active_projects.title: Add the /orient executive-orientation command with a read-only scout agent, and retire /review
active_projects.description:
Add a new `/orient` command that answers "where are we and what next" at executive level, on demand, and retire `/review` in the same change.

PURPOSE. The repository's state is spread across `specs/ROADMAP.md`, `specs/TODO.md`, `specs/state.json`, `specs/CHANGE_LOG.md`, the verdict table in `FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/README.md` (the authority), the C9 and C12 do-not-re-attempt registers in `FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/Verified/Termination/MintBound/Register.lean`, and the wired evidence-probe collection registered in `scripts/check-evidence-probes.sh` (37 wired probes at time of filing). No single artifact answers the orientation question, and reconstructing it by hand is a large, repeated read.

SHAPE. A new command `/orient` backed by a new skill, which dispatches a NEW READ-ONLY SCOUT AGENT. The scout researches current state and returns ONE compressed brief, rendered to the USER as bullet points in conversation. Scout agent tools: Read, Grep, Glob, and Bash for jq and repo scripts. NO Write, NO Edit -- the scout is read-only by construction, not by convention.

REQUIRED BRIEF SECTIONS, in this order, each ruthlessly compressed, none omitted:
(1) WHAT HAPPENED -- the last round(s) of work, verdict-first.
(2) WHY -- the reason each thing was attempted, so that a refutation reads as a result rather than a failure.
(3) WHERE WE ARE -- current position against the stated aim, labelling every item as SETTLED / LANDED-AT-ONE-FIXTURE / CARRIED-UNVERIFIED / OPEN.
(4) GAINS AND LOSSES -- explicitly both. What was bought, including refutations, which close shapes and are successful outcomes in this repository's practice. And what was spent or lost: cycles, routes closed, candidates refuted, blocked acquisitions.
(5) NEXT STRATEGIC GOALS -- the critical path, what gates what, and the cheapest next move.

HARD REQUIREMENTS on the brief:
- Waste no words and omit nothing essential. This is an executive brief, not a report dump.
- Cite durable anchors only -- declaration name, filename, section heading, probe name -- never task numbers, per `.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`.
- Never conflate a SETTLED THEOREM with a LANDED-AT-ONE-FIXTURE result or a CARRIED-UNVERIFIED figure. Conflating these is the single main way this repository's status gets misread, and the four-way label in section (3) exists to prevent it.
- Never present a refutation as a failure.
- Point at the authority README's guardrails rather than restating them.
- Output to the user in conversation rather than producing yet another artifact nobody reads. If any file is written at all, it is one short brief, not a full report.

RETIRE /review, in this same task. Remove its command file, its skill-to-agent mapping row, and its command-reference table row in core's `merge-sources/claudemd.md`.

KEEP `code-reviewer-agent`: already verified at filing time that it has consumers beyond /review's "available for future skill integration" note -- it is referenced by `agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json`, `index-entries.json`, `scripts/validate-index.sh`, `scripts/lint/lint-agent-contracts.sh`, `scripts/validate-context-budgets.sh`, `agents/README.md`, `README.md` and `docs/reference/standards/agent-frontmatter-standard.md`. Removing the agent would break those registry and lint consumers. Re-verify before acting, then leave the agent in place and remove only the /review wiring.

EDIT TARGET. Per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, a consumer repository's `.claude/` tree is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact. Resolve `source_dir` from the consumer's `.claude-extensions.json` and make every change under the source store at the mirroring path -- `agent-system/extensions/core/` for all of these. NEVER hand-author under `.claude/**`. Redeploy afterwards via `deploy-headless.sh` using the bounded-wait idiom (`timeout 540`, Bash tool `timeout` raised to 600000), never a hand-patch of a deployed file.

DELIVERABLES: the new skill definition; the new scout agent definition; the new `/orient` command file; the CLAUDE.md merge-source rows (command-reference table and skill-to-agent mapping); and the /review removal. Register the new skill and agent wherever core's registries require it -- `manifest.json`, `index-entries.json` -- so `validate-index.sh` and `lint-agent-contracts.sh` stay green.

ACCEPTANCE: `/orient` resolves and dispatches the scout; the scout cannot write (no Write/Edit in its frontmatter); the brief carries all five sections with the four-way SETTLED/LANDED-AT-ONE-FIXTURE/CARRIED-UNVERIFIED/OPEN labelling; `/review` is gone from the command reference and the skill mapping; `code-reviewer-agent` is still present and still referenced by its registry consumers; core's own lint and validate scripts pass; the deployed tree is regenerated rather than hand-edited.
=== COORDINATION: REMOVING commands/review.md COLLIDES WITH THE ROADMAP-BATCH LINT RECORD ===
Added 2026-11-02. Nothing else in this record changes.

Removing `agent-system/extensions/core/commands/review.md` deletes a path that is in the declared
file_scope of the record `advisory_lint_for_roadmap_batch_proposals` (not_started), where it is that
record's SEAM B call site -- the place that record's leaning design calls the new lint from. Until
now neither record knew about the other, so whichever lands first silently invalidates the other.

THE file_scope COLLISION GATE CANNOT SEE THIS. Both records live in this same task space and both
name `commands/review.md`, but the conflict is a DELETION-versus-CALL-SITE conflict, not the
concurrent-write conflict the overlap predicate detects. An overlap finding would report "these two
records touch the same file, batch them"; the actual hazard is that one record removes the file the
other plans to edit, which batching alone does not resolve. Record the coordination explicitly
here rather than relying on the gate.

RESOLUTION, both directions:
  - IF THIS RECORD LANDS FIRST (the likely order -- it has no dependencies, while the lint record
    has four): the lint record's seam decision must be re-made against live callers. Its own
    SEAM INVALIDATION section already records this and names the two live options, one of which is
    the `/orient` command this record introduces. No action is required here beyond not being
    surprised: deleting commands/review.md is correct and the other record is already written to
    expect it.
  - IF THE LINT RECORD LANDS FIRST AGAINST commands/review.md: this record must remove the lint
    call alongside the command file rather than orphaning it -- a lint script registered in
    manifest.json with a test companion but no remaining caller. Check for a
    `lint-roadmap-batch-proposals.sh` invocation in commands/review.md before deleting the file,
    and if one is present, decide whether to re-home it on `/orient` or remove the registration
    too.

ALSO NOTE, for this record's own benefit: `/orient` IS READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION, so it REPORTS on
ROADMAP.md and CHANGE_LOG.md state but MAINTAINS neither. The ROADMAP-maintenance gap documented in
a consumer repository's own ROADMAP Maintenance section survives this record intact. Do not read
`/orient` as closing that gap, and do not let the brief's coverage of roadmap state be mistaken for
roadmap upkeep. If section (3) of the brief surfaces stale ROADMAP or CHANGE_LOG content, it says so
and stops there -- repairing it is someone else's work.

active_projects.title: Repair the Zotero sqlite-reconstruction export path: lost CSL fields and a shrink guard calibrated against a corrupt baseline
active_projects.description:
CONTEXT. Three defects in the Zotero export/search path were found and partially worked around by hand. The immediate breakage is already repaired (a correct 1556-entry export is installed and `zotero-export-status.sh` reports it fresh); what remains is the underlying tooling, which will reproduce all three on the next regeneration. Every figure below was MEASURED, not inferred.

DEFECT 1 -- Path 3 (direct sqlite reconstruction) SILENTLY DROPS the CSL fields that container-level search depends on. Measured: an entry emitted by this path carries only `citation-key`, `title`, `author`, `issued`, `keyword`, `abstract`, `attachments`. It carries NO `type`, NO `container-title`, and NO `page`. Consequence, observed directly: a search of the export for "Handbook of Modal Logic" returns zero results, while the SAME query against the live sqlite finds two chapters of that book -- `Higher Order Modal Logic` (Muskens, pp. 621-653, `publicationTitle` = "Handbook of Modal Logic") and `6 Algebras and coalgebras` (pp. 331-426, `publicationTitle` = "Studies in Logic and Practical Reasoning", DOI 10.1016/s1570-2464(07)80009-7). So a chapter-level item is UNFINDABLE by its book or series title through the export, and a user can be told a work is absent from their library when it is present. That is the load-bearing failure: a false negative on an acquisition question. Fix by carrying `type` (from `itemTypes.typeName`), `container-title` (from the `publicationTitle`/`bookTitle` fields), `page`, and `DOI` through the reconstruction into the emitted entries.

DEFECT 2 -- the shrink guard is calibrated against a baseline that may itself be corrupt, and fires as a FALSE POSITIVE when a correct export replaces a bad one. Measured: the previous export held 4042 entries, which is EXACTLY the row count of the sqlite `items` table. It had enumerated every row -- including 1770 attachments, 670 annotations and 62 notes -- as top-level pseudo-entries; 716 of its entries had NO `title` at all. The true bibliographic count is 1556 (`items` minus attachment/annotation/note types, minus `deletedItems`), which is precisely what the reconstruction produced. The guard therefore blocked a CORRECTION as though it were data loss, and `--allow-shrink` -- whose own log line reads "shrink guard bypassed without evaluation" -- was the only way through, which discards the check entirely rather than evaluating it. Make the guard compare like with like: validate baseline quality (e.g. the fraction of entries lacking a title, or an entry count suspiciously equal to the raw `items` row count) before treating it as authoritative, and/or report WHICH items disappeared rather than only a count delta. A count-only comparison between a correct export and a corrupt one carries no information.

DEFECT 3 -- the fallback is reached silently and its degraded shape is not surfaced. The Zotero 7 local API probe returned HTTP 000 (no Zotero process running), so Path 3 was selected automatically. That is correct behaviour, but nothing downstream records that the resulting export is field-poor: `zotero-export-status.sh` reports it simply "fresh", and `zotero-search.sh` returns its zero-results with no indication that container-level fields were never present to match against. A freshness stamp that cannot distinguish "complete" from "reconstructed and field-poor" will keep producing confident false negatives. Record the generating path in `.zotero-library.meta.json` and have the search and status surfaces say so when the export came from reconstruction.

ACCEPTANCE: a reconstruction-path export carries `type`, `container-title`, `page` and `DOI`; searching that export for "Handbook of Modal Logic" finds both chapters named above; the shrink guard distinguishes a correction from a regression and does not require `--allow-shrink` to replace a baseline it can itself detect as corrupt; and the meta stamp plus the search/status surfaces name the generating path when it was reconstruction. Re-verify every measured figure above against the tree as it then stands rather than trusting this description.

NOTE for whoever picks this up: `/home/benjamin/Projects/Literature/zotero-library.json` currently holds the corrected 1556-entry export. A pre-repair copy of the corrupt 4042-entry file was kept only in a session scratchpad and should be assumed gone; the corruption is reproducible by running the generator before this fix lands.

EDIT TARGET. Per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, a consumer repository's `.claude/` tree is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact. Resolve `source_dir` from the consumer's `.claude-extensions.json` and make every change under the source store at the mirroring path -- `agent-system/extensions/literature/` for all of these. NEVER hand-author under `.claude/**`. Redeploy afterwards via the bounded-wait idiom (`timeout 540 bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh`, Bash tool `timeout` raised to 600000), never a hand-patch of a deployed file.

active_projects.title: Dependency edges conflate semantic and serialization rationale, and a semantic edge is filed with no check against landed artifacts
active_projects.description:
CONTEXT. A declared `dependencies[]` edge was filed as a semantic dependency when it was nothing of the kind, and nothing in the authoring path caught it before it cost a full batch run. Measured in the BimodalLogic repository: task 809 declared a dependency on task 734. The edge was refuted on the landed artifacts -- (a) no probe under `specs/evidence/seam-gluing-ray-product/` cross-references the mosaic/`StabSaturated` probe in either direction; (b) the two lines import disjoint `FormalSystem` subtrees (the mosaic probes take the `FormalSystem` root, while 809's inputs resolve to `RaySummary.AnchorLayer`/`LadderModel`); (c) 734's own landed probe header records its predicate as identically true and as deciding nothing about the R2 route; and (d) the paywalled Handbook sections 734 cannot obtain (ch. 11 sections 5.10 "Mosaics" and 5.11 "Monodic fragments") are recorded in the literature-index hazard field itself as the sections the R2 route needs, whereas 809 sits on the R1 ladder line and carries no literature clause at all. Consequence: tasks 809 and 807 were requested in a batch run and never dispatched -- stranded behind an externally-blocked `[HOLD]` whose technical contribution neither of them consumed.

SOURCE RECORD. `/home/benjamin/Projects/BimodalLogic/specs/811_ladder_periodicity_dependency_edge_recut/issues.jsonl`, entry_id `iss_1792217671298_27DB6g` (class `dependency-modeling`, severity `costly`). That file lives in a DIFFERENT repository from this task; read it at the absolute path above rather than looking for it under this repo's `specs/`.

WHAT THE GUIDANCE MUST ADDRESS -- three points, in the authoring path where edges are declared: task creation and any plan/revise path that adds an edge.

1. TWO RATIONALES, ONE FIELD. A `dependencies[]` edge carries either a SEMANTIC rationale (this task consumes a declaration, a result, or a source that the predecessor produces) or a SERIALIZATION rationale (the two tasks have an unordered `file_scope` overlap and must not land in one wave). The two are not interchangeable, and the field expresses both today with nothing recording which -- so a serialization edge reads as a semantic block, and an audit cannot tell them apart without re-deriving the whole question. The vocabulary already exists and the distinction is already partly visible but never persisted: `docs/reference/standards/multi-task-creation-standard.md`'s "Auto-Derived Dependency Annotation" rule requires a Component-4a-added edge to be annotated `(auto: file overlap)` in the Component 7 *confirmation summary* only; `context/patterns/multi-task-operations.md`'s "File Footprint Overlap as a Serialization Edge" section states flatly that wave assignment "treats any `dependencies[]` edge as a serialization constraint"; and `context/reference/state-management-schema.md`'s `dependencies` row reads only "Task numbers that must complete before this task can start", with the serializing-edge derivation described a section later under `file_scope`. None of it survives into `state.json`. Live precedent from the same run: the surviving 807 -> 809 edge is a genuine serialization edge with no semantic content, and its rationale had to be re-labelled by hand in an audit report precisely because the edge itself cannot carry the distinction.

2. A SEMANTIC EDGE SHOULD BE CHECKABLE AT THE POINT IT IS FILED. The guidance should require a semantic edge to name what is consumed -- which declaration, which file, or which source section -- rather than being asserted from topical or lexical proximity. Name the specific trap this case fell into, because it is the generalizable part: the two tasks were adjacent in vocabulary but not in content. 734's live half is stab WITNESSING (an SH1 witness-direction predicate over a chosen mosaic set); 809's gate 8 is stab SELF-REFERENCE (a definability fixpoint obstruction on a coprime-cycle object). Shared vocabulary, different objects, different fixtures, neither feeding the other. Note also the asymmetry against `file_scope`: Component 4a's own guidance tells an author to over-declare rather than under-declare, because a missed collision serializes silently while a false one costs only an orchestration wave. For a semantic edge the asymmetry runs the OTHER way -- a spurious semantic edge is the expensive error. The two conventions must not be stated as one rule.

3. WHY THIS WARRANTS GUIDANCE RATHER THAN A ONE-OFF CORRECTION -- the cost asymmetry. An unchecked semantic edge onto a task that later goes to `[HOLD]` silently converts every transitive successor into a non-dispatchable task, and that failure is invisible from any single task's own record: it surfaces only at a batch run's conclusion stage, which is where this one was finally caught. The guidance should say this plainly, since it is the reason an author should spend the check at filing time rather than deferring it.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, deliberately not pre-decided here: whether closing point 1 needs only prose at the authoring sites, or a recorded discriminator that survives into `state.json` -- e.g. a per-edge rationale, which `dependencies[]`'s flat integer-array shape cannot hold without a schema change, and which `scripts/update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add` would then have to accept and `scripts/validate-state.sh` to tolerate. Rule on it during research/plan from the measured cost of each option against the number of consumers that read `dependencies[]`; a prose-only outcome is an acceptable and possibly correct answer.

SCOPE NOTE -- DO NOT RE-FIX THE EDGES. The corrective edge change is already landed and committed in BimodalLogic: 809's dependencies are now `[805]`, the 807 -> 809 serialization edge is preserved, and task 734's hold, probe and report are untouched. This task is about the authoring guidance that would have prevented the mis-filing, not about redoing that correction.

ACCEPTANCE. (1) The semantic/serialization distinction is stated once in a single canonical location and referenced by path from every authoring site that declares or adds an edge, never restated at each site. (2) The authoring path for a semantic edge requires naming the consumed declaration, file, or source section at the point the edge is filed. (3) The `[HOLD]`-transitivity cost is recorded as the stated reason for the check. (4) Re-verify every file path, section heading, and quoted line cited above against the tree as it then stands rather than trusting this description.

EDIT TARGET. Per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, a consumer repository's `.claude/` tree is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact. Make every change under the source store at `agent-system/extensions/core/` at the path mirroring the deployed one -- NEVER hand-author under `.claude/**`. Redeploy afterwards via the bounded-wait idiom (`timeout 540 bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh`, Bash tool `timeout` raised to 600000), never a hand-patch of a deployed file.

active_projects.title: Take the Lean Challenge snapshot in the plan phase, where it is still meaningful, instead of leaving it to an implement phase the status gate correctly refuses
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/lean/** (primarily) and agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation over BimodalLogic:#761 (ladder realization theorem), user-approved at the lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. FILED HERE, NOT IN BIMODALLOGIC: an agent-system change belongs in the repository that owns the source store, per the mis-siting correction recorded under this repo's #390 and the authoring hole recorded under #391. All issue-log citations below are entry_ids in the ORIGINATING repository's log, BimodalLogic:specs/761_ladder_realization_theorem/issues.jsonl -- the identifier #761 is a BimodalLogic number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json. Cross-repo overlap has no mechanical representation today (#401); where it matters below it is stated in prose.

CITATIONS -- two entries, one cause, seven days apart:
  BimodalLogic:#761:iss_1792362555851_OvmVEP  (class tooling-refusal, severity minor, implement, dispatch_seq 6) -- the refusal itself.
  BimodalLogic:#761:iss_1791770495965_TM78BN  (class gate-baseline, severity minor, implement, dispatch_seq 3) -- the downstream consequence, recorded FIRST and independently.

PROVENANCE OF THE FIGURES BELOW: every file, line number, and quoted string in the ROOT CAUSE sections was re-derived by direct read of the source store at creation time (2026-10-18), not copied from the originating report. Line numbers move -- re-derive before editing. The incident narratives and measured costs are CARRIED-UNVERIFIED from the cited issues.jsonl entries; they are not re-measurable from this repository, since the incidents happened in BimodalLogic.

LIVE SYMPTOM -- the snapshot is unobtainable by the time anything asks for it, so a per-phase drift check degrades to hand-diffing. Per the cited entries:
- `lean-challenge-snapshot.sh 761 .` refused with exit 73 because the task's status was already 'implementing'. The plan's Phase 1 had asked for the snapshot precisely so that `--check` would be available to the later phases.
- THE REFUSAL IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE WEAKENED. The implementer declined to pass --force, on the stated ground that the tool's own banner says a post-implementation Challenge certifies nothing, so a forced manifest would be MISLEADING PROVENANCE in git history. That judgment is right and this record endorses it.
- Consequence, from the earlier entry: `--check` exited 71 at a later phase (no manifest at the task directory's challenge/manifest.json, because the snapshot was never taken at plan time), so the advisory drift check could not run for ANY phase. Three Goal signatures were instead diffed byte-for-byte against the plan's Lean Challenge Statements block by hand. They matched -- so nothing was certified wrongly; the loss is that the mechanical check was replaced by a manual one that does not scale and leaves no artifact.

ROOT CAUSE -- the snapshot has no owner in the lifecycle. Verified in the source store at creation time:
- scripts/lean-challenge-snapshot.sh hard-codes PRE_IMPLEMENTATION_STATUSES="not_started researching researched planning planned" and refuses every later status (implementing, pr_ready, completed, blocked, partial, abandoned, expanded) with exit 73, on the documented ground that "a Challenge must predate implementation to certify anything". --force exists only as a loud, incident-shaped bypass, never a silent one. All of this is correct.
- The producing side exists too: context/formats/plan-format.md carries `## Lean Challenge Statements (format, lean/lean4 plans only)`, whose own text says the section exists "so a downstream tool (lean-challenge-snapshot.sh) can turn a plan into a trusted, immutable Challenge module BEFORE the implementation agent runs".
- NOTHING INVOKES IT. extensions/lean/manifest.json has a top-level `hooks` value of null -- the lean extension registers no lifecycle hooks at any stage. So the only thing that ever asks for a snapshot is a plan that writes "take the snapshot" into a phase body, which by construction executes during IMPLEMENT, which is exactly the status the gate refuses. The design record already identifies the plan as the authoritative Challenge source (its R1-vs-R2 ruling makes plan-declared statements primary and git-baseline extraction a loudly-degraded fallback for legacy plans only), so the data is in hand at plan time; only the invocation is missing.

SCOPE -- make the plan phase's own postflight take the snapshot for lean/lean4 tasks whose plan carries a non-empty `## Lean Challenge Statements` section. Determine the right registration point and record why:
(a) a `postflight` lifecycle hook declared in extensions/lean/manifest.json's top-level `hooks` object (see docs/guides/creating-extensions.md for the hook schema and execution contract) -- extension-local, which is where lean-specific behaviour belongs, but note that the lean extension currently registers no hooks at all, so this establishes the pattern and must be verified to actually fire;
(b) a gated call from core's plan-cycle postflight (scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh) -- guaranteed to run, but puts lean-specific knowledge in core, which is the wrong direction unless (a) is demonstrated unworkable.
Prefer (a); fall back to (b) only with the reason recorded.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- DO NOT weaken the exit-73 status gate, and do not add an automatic --force anywhere. The gate is the reason the refusal was trustworthy; a snapshot taken at the right time makes the gate irrelevant rather than wrong.
- The hook MUST be non-blocking. A plan phase must never fail because a snapshot could not be taken. Absence of a manifest already degrades gracefully -- `--check` exits 71 and the drift check is advisory -- so the correct failure mode is a warning plus no manifest, exactly as today.
- The hook MUST be inert for a task that is not lean/lean4, and inert for a lean4 plan that commits to no theorem. THAT SECOND CASE IS NOT YET DEFINED: #385 exists precisely to define the sanctioned shape for a zero-theorem lean4 plan and to make this same script distinguish it from a malformed one. Until that ruling lands, a hook added here would fire on exactly the undefined case. This is why #385 is a hard dependency, not a courtesy edge.
- Idempotence and immutability: re-running the plan postflight (a revision, a second plan cycle) must not silently overwrite an existing Challenge manifest. The design record's immutability mechanism is load-bearing -- a Challenge the agent can rewrite certifies nothing. Decide and record what a re-plan does: refuse, version, or require an explicit regeneration.

VERIFY:
- Extend scripts/tests/test-lean-challenge-snapshot.sh (and/or add a hook test): the hook fires for a lean4 task with a populated Challenge section and produces a manifest under the task directory's challenge/ subdirectory; a later `--check` from an implement phase then exits 0 rather than 71.
- Pin that the hook is inert for a non-lean task type, and that a plan-phase hook failure does not fail the plan phase.
- Pin that the exit-73 status gate and its PRE_IMPLEMENTATION_STATUSES set are UNCHANGED, and that --force still warns in its incident-shaped form.
- Pin the re-plan behaviour chosen above in both directions.

TERRITORY EDGES:
- 385 (HARD SEMANTIC DEPENDENCY, not merely serialization): same two lean files (lean-challenge-snapshot.sh and its design record challenge-snapshot.md) plus core/context/formats/plan-format.md. It defines the sanctioned shape for a lean4 plan that commits to no theorem and makes the script distinguish it from a malformed one. A hook added before that ruling fires on an undefined case and will mis-handle it. 385 MUST land first.
- No edge on 328: its file_scope covers lean/agents/, lean/commands/, lean/rules/ and lean/skills/ but NOT lean/scripts/ or lean/scripts/tests/, so there is no collision with this record's targets. Checked explicitly rather than assumed.

DUPLICATE CHECK PERFORMED. 385 is the only open task touching these files and is a dependency rather than a duplicate -- it governs WHICH plans the tool must accept; this record governs WHEN the tool is called. 396 and 412 (lean-extension) were checked and do not name these files. No absorption candidate found.

ADDITIONAL TERRITORY EDGES, SURFACED MECHANICALLY BY validate-state.sh AFTER THIS RECORD WAS WRITTEN (declared with labelled rationale rather than as bare numbers, per the open concern that dependency edges conflate semantic and serialization rationale -- see #438):
- 435 (SERIALIZATION only, OPERATOR-LIFTABLE): declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ coarsely, which covers this record's one core target, scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (relevant only if registration option (b) is chosen; if option (a), the manifest hook, is taken, this edge is moot and should be lifted).
ALL EDGES IN THIS PARAGRAPH ARE SERIALIZATION-ONLY AND OPERATOR-LIFTABLE. They exist because the OTHER record declares a coarse directory rather than because this record's targets are contested; validate-state.sh flags each as a "Coarse file_scope declaration" warning against that other record. An operator who confirms the predecessor does not touch this record's named files may lift any of them with update-task-status.sh --depends-on-remove.

=== SECOND INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, DIFFERENT REPOSITORY, DIFFERENT CAUSE-PATH ===
Added by the conclusion stage (channel b, user-approved at the lead level) of an /orchestrate invocation in the Logos/Theory repository. ABSORBED INTO THIS RECORD rather than filed as a new task: the scope below is the scope this record already owns.

CITATION: Logos/Theory:358:iss_1793952707617_rX6BDM. The identifier 358 is a Logos/Theory task number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json; the entry lives in that repo's own issue log. Cross-repo overlap still has no mechanical representation (see the cross-repo source-store gate-blindness record).

WHAT THIS CITATION ADDS THAT THE BIMODALLOGIC PAIR DOES NOT. The BimodalLogic entries show the snapshot being REFUSED at implement time (exit 73, status already 'implementing'). This one shows the weaker and more common failure: nobody even reached a refusal. No manifest existed at the task directory's challenge/manifest.json because no plan-phase site ever takes a snapshot, so --check had nothing to verify against and the pinned-signature check simply never ran. The defect is therefore STRUCTURAL, not a per-task sequencing slip: on every lean4 task to date, --check has provided no value, because the producing side is unowned rather than mistimed.

MEASURED COST (carried-unverified in this repository; re-derive or re-cite at plan time): pinned-signature fidelity was verified BY HAND against the plan's `## Lean Challenge Statements` section -- 13 Goals identifiers, four pinned null-state signatures plus sound_c4-c7 and valid_m1/m2. They matched, so nothing was certified wrongly; the loss is again that a mechanical check was replaced by a manual one that leaves no artifact and does not scale. Because the verdict is advisory, the gate did not fail -- it simply reported nothing.

=== FACTS RE-DERIVED BY DIRECT READ OF THE SOURCE STORE AT AMENDMENT TIME (2026-11-06; line numbers drift, re-derive before editing) ===
- `--check` HAS NO CALL SITE ANYWHERE. The only reference to it in the whole lean extension is prose in rules/plan-compliance.md's "Mechanical check" paragraph (~L56). No skill, agent, hook, or script invokes it. The script's own header states this itself: "This script is a standalone CLI, not wired into any completion gate by this script or by anything else in this source tree."
- Both implementation agents DO read the manifest, but only behind `--compare`: lean-implementation-agent.md (~L389) and lean-implementation-hard-agent.md (~L522) each resolve `specs/${padded_num}_${project_name}/challenge/manifest.json` and, when it is absent, emit the advisory `challenge_missing` preflight verdict. Neither ever runs `--check`. So wiring the producing side at plan time is necessary but NOT sufficient for the symptom in this citation: the consuming side needs a `--check` call site too. STATE WHICH PHASE OWNS THAT CALL and record why.
- The manifest LOCATION question named in the originating change request is already settled and must not be relitigated: `specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/challenge/manifest.json`, per the design record's "Manifest Schema" section, and both implementation agents already hard-code exactly that path. The open part is only the zero-goal case, where exit 72 is a side-effect-free early exit that produces no manifest by design.
- REGISTRATION-SITE EVIDENCE, sharpening option (a) vs (b) above. extensions/lean/manifest.json has NO top-level `hooks` key at all (not a null value). The hook mechanism itself is live and proven: skill-base.sh's `skill_run_extension_hook` accepts the stages preflight|context_injection|verification|postflight, reads them from a manifest's top-level `hooks` object, and is in production use by the nix extension (preflight, context_injection) and the nvim extension (context_injection). Its invocation signature is `"$task_number" "$task_type" "$task_dir" "$session_id" "$operation"`, so a single `postflight` hook can discriminate the plan phase from the implement phase on `$operation` -- which is what makes option (a) able to serve both the producing and the consuming call site from one registration. Hooks are already non-blocking by construction (a non-zero exit is logged as a warning and execution continues), which satisfies this record's non-blocking hard constraint for free.
- HOOK RESOLUTION PRECONDITION, AND A STALE COMMENT THAT CONTRADICTS IT. `skill_run_extension_hook` resolves a declared hook to `.claude/scripts/$(basename "$hook_script")` and skips it with a loud NOTE if that path is missing or not executable. Deployment is therefore load-bearing for option (a). lean-challenge-snapshot.sh IS listed in manifest.json's provides.scripts and IS deployed executable into consumer trees (verified in Logos/Theory at amendment time), BUT the script's own repo-root-resolution comment (~L96-100) asserts the opposite: "this script is not itself deployed as a Claude Code artifact -- see manifest.json". That parenthetical is factually wrong and directly misleads anyone reasoning about hook reachability. CORRECT IT as part of this work.
- The CWD convention in that same comment block is a real constraint on any hook: the script resolves `specs/` relative to the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY and takes `project_root` as a separate argument. A hook must therefore be invoked from the repo root that owns the specs/ directory, and must pass the target Lean project root explicitly. Pin this in the hook test.

=== ADDITIONAL SUB-QUESTION TO SETTLE, NOT COVERED BY THIS RECORD OR ITS SIBLINGS ===
WHETHER `--check` SHOULD STAY ADVISORY-ONLY OR BECOME BLOCKING once a manifest is reliably present. This is explicitly a non-goal of the --check scope-limit record ("Do not relitigate the advisory-vs-blocking status of the --check verdict") and is not addressed here either: this record's own non-blocking constraint is about the PLAN-PHASE HOOK's failure mode, a different question from the IMPLEMENT-PHASE DRIFT VERDICT's strength. The originating change request asks for it to be settled, so settle it here with the reason recorded, in whichever direction.
  - Arguments were deliberately not pre-decided. If promoted: the advisory stance is asserted in THREE places that must move together -- the script's own GATE STRENGTH header block, rules/plan-compliance.md's "ADVISORY ONLY" paragraph, and the design record's `## Gate Strength: Advisory Only` section. The escalation route already exists in that rule (mark the phase [BLOCKED] and raise it; never quietly edit the recorded Challenge to match the implementation), so promotion needs no new escalation mechanism.
  - If promoted, a precondition is that the false-ambiguity defect owned by the --check scope-limit record is fixed FIRST: a blocking check that fails on a correct tree because a research prototype under specs/ declares a pinned name would be worse than no check. That makes the scope-limit record a hard ordering constraint on PROMOTION specifically, even though it currently depends on this one for the invocation point. If both land here, sequence them explicitly; if promotion is deferred, say so and leave the verdict advisory.
  - A defensible outcome is to decline promotion and record why. The deliverable is a recorded ruling, not necessarily a stronger gate.

=== FILE SCOPE ADDITION ===
rules/plan-compliance.md is added to file_scope: its "Mechanical check" paragraph is the only existing reference to --check anywhere, and it is one of the three places the advisory stance is asserted. Either outcome of the sub-question above edits it. The two implementation agent files (lean-implementation-agent.md, lean-implementation-hard-agent.md) are NOT added to file_scope, because whether they gain a --check call site depends on which registration option wins; if option (b) or a per-agent call site is chosen, declare them at plan time.

active_projects.title: Require a verification criterion over a repo-wide gate with standing pre-existing findings to be baseline-relative, not absolute
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (primarily) and agent-system/extensions/lean/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation over BimodalLogic:#761 (ladder realization theorem), user-approved at the lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. FILED HERE, NOT IN BIMODALLOGIC: an agent-system change belongs in the repository that owns the source store, per the mis-siting correction recorded under this repo's #390 and the authoring hole recorded under #391. All issue-log citations below are entry_ids in the ORIGINATING repository's log, BimodalLogic:specs/761_ladder_realization_theorem/issues.jsonl -- the identifier #761 is a BimodalLogic number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json. Cross-repo overlap has no mechanical representation today (#401); where it matters below it is stated in prose.

CITATIONS -- two independent cases, two different gates, six days apart:
  BimodalLogic:#761:iss_1791769990070_9Nl16r  (class gate-baseline, severity minor, implement, dispatch_seq 3) -- the repo-wide task-reference lint.
  BimodalLogic:#761:iss_1792364282512_jWKKvT  (class verification-criterion, severity minor, implement, dispatch_seq 6) -- the vacuous-definition grep.
A third entry in the same log (iss_1791770495965_TM78BN) records the vacuous-pattern case a second time from the earlier phase, so the grep case recurred across dispatches rather than being a one-off.

PROVENANCE OF THE FIGURES BELOW: every file, line number, and quoted string in the ROOT CAUSE sections was re-derived by direct read of the source store at creation time (2026-10-18), not copied from the originating report. Line numbers move -- re-derive before editing. The incident narratives and measured costs are CARRIED-UNVERIFIED from the cited issues.jsonl entries; they are not re-measurable from this repository, since the incidents happened in BimodalLogic.

LIVE SYMPTOM -- a plan demanded an absolute gate result the tree cannot produce, so a correctly-passing phase had to report a non-conforming verdict:
(a) "repo-wide check-task-references.sh --quiet exits 0". MEASURED: it exits 1 on 198 pre-existing occurrences in Boneyard/*/README.md (archived code), NONE in any file the task touched; every touched file passes individually and the per-file checks pass. The criterion is unattainable without an out-of-scope archive cleanup.
(b) "vacuous-definition grep count 0", asserted repeatedly across phases. MEASURED: the tree carries one PRE-EXISTING hit at HEAD -- FormalSystem/Examples/TemporalStructures.lean:495, int_domain_universal -- whose `:= trivial` closes a REAL goal (membership in the universal domain is True by definition). So the hit is not even a finding; it is a correct declaration that matches the pattern.
Both had to be reported as baseline-unchanged rather than as the stated criterion. The cost is not a wrong result -- it is that a conforming phase produces a verdict that does not match its own plan, which is indistinguishable on first read from a phase that failed its gate, and so costs a triage pass and erodes the verdict's meaning.

ROOT CAUSE -- the authoring standard has every adjacent rule except this one. Verified in the source store at creation time (around these lines; re-derive before editing):
- context/formats/plan-format.md's `### Naming a tool's entry point in verification criteria` (around line 498) is the closest existing rule and is strikingly near-miss. It MANDATES naming the repository's sanctioned entry point rather than a bare binary, and it MANDATES checking the invoked command's exit status rather than relying on a stdout diff against a baseline -- because "a tool broken identically on both sides of that diff makes 'no new findings' vacuously true". So the file already reasons about baselines, and already warns about one specific way a baseline-relative criterion goes wrong, while never stating when a criterion MUST be baseline-relative in the first place. Its declared enforcement level is advisory prose only, with no corresponding validate-artifact.sh check.
- `### Counts-are-hypotheses obligation` (around line 422) makes any count, file list, or scope estimate a hypothesis carrying a `**Scope Hypothesis**:` line stating how to confirm it at implementation time. That is the right shape for a FORWARD-LOOKING estimate; a standing pre-existing finding count is a different object -- a measurable property of HEAD that should be measured ONCE at plan time and then held fixed as the comparison point.
- `## Verification Tiers` (around line 260) defines how BROADLY verification must run (prose < local < interface < full) and requires the final phase to take the `full` tier, whose in-phase verification is "the complete gate set for the repository". So the format compels a repo-wide run at the final phase while saying nothing about how to phrase the criterion for a repo-wide gate that is not green at HEAD. The two halves do not meet.
- A grep of plan-format.md for baseline / pre-existing / unchanged finds only incidental uses: the stdout-diff warning above, and tier prose using 'unchanged' in an unrelated sense. There is no rule to amend here -- there is a rule to ADD, sited next to the entry-point rule it completes.

SCOPE -- add the baseline-relative criterion rule to plan-format.md, sited as a sibling of `### Naming a tool's entry point in verification criteria`, and propagate it to the planner's own contract. The rule must state at least:
- WHEN it binds: whenever a phase's verification criterion invokes a gate whose scope exceeds the phase's edit scope (a repo-wide lint, a tree-wide grep, an aggregate sweep) AND that gate is not green at the task's starting commit.
- WHAT the criterion must then say: a baseline-relative verdict -- 'no NEW findings relative to the recorded baseline', or 'baseline-unchanged at N' -- never an absolute 'exits 0' or 'count is 0'.
- WHERE the baseline comes from: measured at PLAN time against the task's starting commit and recorded IN the plan, so the implementer compares against a number the plan committed to rather than one it discovers mid-phase and could rationalize. Pair this with the existing counts-are-hypotheses and carried-figure obligations rather than restating them.
- The ESCAPE HATCH, stated explicitly: an absolute criterion remains correct and preferred when the gate IS green at the starting commit, and a plan may legitimately demand an absolute result as a deliberate in-scope cleanup -- in which case the cleanup is part of the task's scope and must appear in a phase's Files to modify.
Then rule on enforcement: whether validate-artifact.sh can mechanically flag an absolute criterion naming a known repo-wide gate, or whether this stays advisory prose like its sibling rule. Record the ruling either way; a mechanical check here is only worth having if it can avoid false-flagging the legitimate absolute case above.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT make this a license to lower a gate. 'No new findings' must mean the gate still RUNS at full repo scope and its exit status is still checked -- the sibling entry-point rule is explicit that a stdout-diff-only comparison makes 'no new findings' vacuously true when the tool is broken identically on both sides. Whatever wording lands must preserve that warning and must not be satisfiable by a diff alone.
- Do NOT restate the carried-figure or counts-are-hypotheses conventions. report-format.md's `## Carried-Figure Discipline` is the authoritative home for carried figures for BOTH reports and plans, and plan-format.md already POINTS there rather than restating, deliberately so the two cannot drift. A recorded baseline figure is a measurement this plan makes, so say how it interacts with those conventions and point; do not fork them.
- Keep every existing heading string in plan-format.md unchanged; several have consumers (validate-artifact.sh, plan-file-scope-harvest.sh reads `Files to modify`, and the lean-gated `## Lean Challenge Statements` section).
- If a mechanical check is added, it MUST fail open and advisory-first. A false flag on a legitimate absolute criterion would push planners toward vaguer criteria, which is worse than the defect being fixed.

VERIFY:

LIVE SYMPTOM -- `literature-search.sh` returned degraded=true with NO results for a quasimodel query, and the research agent fell back to grepping the corpus source directory directly for the specific theorem and definition numbers it needed. The workaround succeeded, so nothing was lost on this run; what the entry records is that the agent had to invent the fallback, because the tool told it retrieval had degraded and then told it nothing about what to do next.

ROOT CAUSE -- the degraded signal is produced honestly and then dropped in exactly the case where it is most actionable. Verified in the source store at creation time:
- scripts/literature-search.sh computes `degraded = fallback_tier != 'bm25'` and emits it in the result envelope alongside fallback_tier and query_error. Its own comment states the intent precisely: degraded is "the honest, never-silent signal that distinguishes 'retrieval degraded' from 'genuine zero-result', which literature-briefing.sh consumes downstream". The producer is correct and this record does not fault it.
- When the merged result set is EMPTY, that same code sets `fallback_tier = 'none'`, which makes `degraded` TRUE. So the zero-result case is reported as degraded by construction -- which is the honest reading (no tier answered), but it also means degraded=true with zero results is the single most common degraded shape, not an edge case.
- scripts/literature-briefing.sh is the consumer, and its degraded banner is emitted under the guard `if [ "$degraded" = "true" ] && [ "${#briefing_lines[@]}" -gt 0 ]`. The second conjunct is the defect: the banner requires that there BE results. It carries three well-written variants -- a trigram-fallback warning, a phrase-retry warning after an FTS5 syntax error, and a generic fallback_tier warning -- and each ends by telling the agent to verify relevance itself, which is advice that only makes sense when rows exist.
- Net: in the cited case (degraded=true, fallback_tier='none', zero rows) the briefing emits NO banner and NO directive at all. The signal the producer went to trouble to make never-silent is silent precisely when the agent has nothing else to go on.

SCOPE -- give the zero-result degraded case its own banner and a usable directive, in literature-briefing.sh. The directive should say what the agent in the cited incident worked out by itself, so the next agent does not have to:
- distinguish 'the corpus has nothing on this' from 'the index did not answer this query', and say which one the tool can and cannot tell apart;
- name the sanctioned next steps rather than leaving them to invention -- at minimum re-querying with narrower or alternative terms (the --multi mode exists for per-term recall in one process), consulting --toc / --doc to navigate by document structure instead of ranking, and, as the explicit last resort, reading the corpus source directly;
- state whether an index-health problem is indicated and where that is checked (`/literature --validate`, and the index-health mode of `/literature`).
Also rule on whether `fallback_tier = 'none'` on an empty result set should remain folded into `degraded`, or be reported as its own distinguishable state. Do not change the producer's semantics without recording the reasoning: downstream consumers read the field, and the current definition is deliberate.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Preserve the three existing banner variants verbatim in their current cases (trigram_fallback, phrase_retry, generic). This record ADDS a fourth case; it does not rewrite the working ones.
- Preserve backward compatibility of the envelope reader. literature-briefing.sh already accepts a legacy bare-array shape and two envelope shapes; whatever lands must keep all three readable and must not fail when degraded/fallback_tier/query_error are absent.
- `query_error` is a DIFFERENT condition from `degraded` -- the producer documents it as non-null only when every sub-query failed against every database that exists. A genuine query error must not be collapsed into the new zero-result banner; if anything it deserves a louder one.
- The banner is guidance, not a gate. Nothing here may make a research dispatch fail or block on degraded retrieval.
- No task-number references in the banner text or the context file -- it lands under agent-system/**.

VERIFY:
- Add a literature/scripts/tests/ case covering the cited shape: degraded=true, fallback_tier='none', zero rows -> a banner and a directive ARE emitted. Pin the negative too: a healthy bm25 answer with rows emits NO banner.
- Pin that each of the three existing variants still fires in its own case with its existing wording.
- Pin that all three accepted envelope shapes still parse, including the legacy bare array with no degraded field.
- Reproduce the cited case end-to-end if the corpus allows: a query that no tier answers should now produce actionable text rather than silence.

The team lead flagged a stall and the gate was re-run in the foreground, producing the identical result (exit 0, 31 PASS) at a MEASURED cost of about 5 minutes plus the stall triage. The implementer recorded the lesson in the entry itself: for a gate whose result is needed in the same turn, run it in the foreground within the tool timeout.

FIRST OBLIGATION OF THIS RECORD: DETERMINE WHETHER IT IS ALREADY FIXED, AND CLOSE AS NO-CHANGE IF SO. The incident is dated 2026-10-12. This repository's #376 -- "Lean implementation agents mandate the detach-then-await-notification path core forbids, stranding dispatches mid-phase" -- is COMPLETED, with a last_updated of 2026-10-17, and its file_scope includes context/patterns/bounded-build-waiter.md and all four lean agent definitions. So the cited incident PREDATES that fix by five days, and the agent that hit it was running the pre-fix lean contract. Research MUST first establish whether the landed wording already governs this case. If it does, close this record as no-change with the finding recorded -- that is a successful outcome here, not a failure.

WHAT IS NEVERTHELESS NOT COVERED, AS FAR AS A SOURCE-STORE READ AT CREATION TIME CAN TELL (re-derive; line numbers move):
- The existing foreground-preference rule is keyed on DURATION, not on when the result is needed. context/patterns/bounded-build-waiter.md's `## The Canonical Idiom` (around line 99) says "Prefer the simpler foreground form, `timeout 3000 cmd`, whenever the command fits within the" per-call ceiling, and goes on (around lines 103-106) to warn that preferring the foreground form for anything longer than two minutes REQUIRES raising that timeout, since otherwise it reproduces the very failure the file's idiom exists to avoid. That is a cost-and-fit test. The cited lesson is a DIFFERENT test -- do I need this answer before this turn ends -- and it can select the foreground form even for a command whose duration would otherwise argue for detaching.
- The forbidden path is stated as ending a turn on an UNRESOLVED wait. The canonical agent-contract bullet (around lines 201-207) forbids using run_in_background or a Monitor to watch a local gate from within a dispatched subagent, and forbids ever ending "the turn on an unresolved local background wait", on the ground that the harness's asynchronous detach-then-await-notification path hands the dispatch back unfinished. In the cited incident the wait RESOLVED and the notification ARRIVED -- the failure was that it was not CONSUMED before the turn ended. A strict reading of 'unresolved' does not cover that.
- bounded-build-waiter.md carries a `## Shape Taxonomy: Three Ways a Wait Goes Wrong, Distinguished by Trigger` section (around line 440) enumerating three shapes, the third being harness-initiated backgrounding of an ordinary foreground call. An arrived-but-unconsumed completion notification is a candidate FOURTH shape, distinguished by its own trigger, and the taxonomy is the natural home for it.
- context/patterns/external-process-wait.md's six Required Rules and its `## Local vs. Remote Waits` section (around line 162) govern long remote waits (its rule 3 already forbids run_in_background and Monitor for CI waits inside a subagent). A grep of that file for 'same turn' / 'this turn' returns nothing.

SCOPE -- deliberately small, and prose-only:
(1) State the result-needed-this-turn criterion where the foreground/detach choice is actually made, as an ADDITIONAL and independent reason to take the foreground form, alongside the existing fits-the-ceiling reason. Make clear it can override the duration-based preference, and say what to do when the command genuinely cannot fit the ceiling AND the result is needed this turn (the honest answer is probably: raise the timeout per the existing guidance, or restructure so the result is not needed this turn -- never detach and hope).
(2) Add the arrived-but-unconsumed notification to the Shape Taxonomy as a fourth shape with its own trigger, so the diagnosis is nameable. One sentence of remedy, pointing at (1).
(3) Cross-reference from external-process-wait.md's `## Local vs. Remote Waits` so a reader who arrives at the remote-wait file first is not told a local same-turn gate may be detached.
NOTHING IS BROKEN IN ANY SCRIPT and this is not a data-repair record. The deliverable is guidance prose in the core source store plus any index wiring it needs.

- Do NOT weaken the livelock protection that detachment exists to provide. #376's own record is explicit that lean's underlying concern -- a killed build caches no artifact, so retries restart at the same module and livelock -- may well be sound, and that the correct shape keeps detachment while fixing the WAIT step. Adding a same-turn criterion must not become a blanket 'always foreground'.

Its stated rationale is that a plan harvesting a `.lean` path but omitting these "either blocks on the pre-commit typst-sync-check.sh gate or fails check-module-invariants.sh's INV check mid-implementation -- this has happened twice independently". A `generated_surfaces_available()` predicate gates the whole stage on both repository scripts existing, so the behaviour is inert in a repository that carries neither generator, and `generated_inventory_readmes()` deliberately mirrors the gate's own BEGIN_RE/fence/dir= parsing.
So the INV half of the cited incident is a MISS BY AN EXISTING MECHANISM, not a new concern: the stage exists precisely to make stale inventory blocks a declared consequence. Determine FIRST why it did not cover this case -- whether the wiring edit harvested no `.lean` path, whether the ancestor-chain walk missed the new module's READMEs, or whether the stage simply does not run on the plan shape used -- and fix that. That finding is the primary deliverable.

SCOPE -- narrow, and bounded by what belongs in the agent system:
(1) Establish and record why the existing generated-surface appending did not cover the four stale inventory blocks, and close that gap if it is a gap. If the stage behaved correctly and the plan simply harvested no `.lean` path, say so and stop -- do not manufacture a fix.
(2) Rule on whether the OTHER three failure classes (a lint-suppression allowlist entry, an identifier-naming check, a suppression-needs-a-reason check) belong in this stage at all. ARGUE IT BOTH WAYS AND RECORD THE RULING. Against: the stage's single documented job is appending GENERATED SURFACES a `.lean` edit forces regeneration of, and a nolints.json entry or a rename is not a generated surface -- widening the stage to 'things the gate will probably complain about' would blur a crisp contract and invite repository-specific guesswork into core. For: all four arise from the same act (wiring a module), the stage already carries repository-specific knowledge of this very gate, and a one-line pre-flag costs far less than a fix-up pass. A defensible outcome here is 'no, and here is why' -- record it rather than widening by default.
(3) THE REPOSITORY-LOCAL HALF IS OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS RECORD. The actual remedies for C16, C23 and C29 -- scripts/nolints.json entries, the rename, the reason block -- and the human-facing wiring directive that would warn about them live in the BimodalLogic repository (its scripts/check-module-invariants.sh, scripts/nolints.json, docs/project-info/MAINTENANCE.md and ORGANISATION.md all reference this gate). Those are not agent-system files and must not be edited from this record. If ruling (2) concludes the warning belongs in a human-facing wiring directive rather than in core's harvest stage, the correct outcome is to say so and have a BimodalLogic-local record created for it -- not to reach across the boundary.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:

- Do NOT let `generated_inventory_readmes()` drift from the gate it mirrors. Its header states it mirrors check-module-invariants.sh's own BEGIN_RE/fence/dir= parsing and deliberately NOT its rows=/cols=/filter=/sort= rendering semantics. Keep that boundary and keep the comment accurate.

This is the third independent occurrence of the failure plan-file-scope-harvest.sh's own header says

SURFACE A -- typst/generated/status.typ. iss_1793832006386_cqjHI0, class gate-collision, severity

active_projects.title: Repo-specific content has leaked into the shared agent-system source store
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/{formal,lean}/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Resolve source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one. REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh to RESULT=landed_verify_clean. No task-number references in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md) and no record-versioning language (rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

GOAL. Repository-specific content from one consuming Lean project has leaked into the SHARED agent-system source store, so every other repository deploying the formal or lean extension receives context files asserting facts about a Lean tree it does not have. Resolve the four affected files, choosing PER FILE between relocation and de-specialization, and record the grounds that settled each choice.

THE ROUTE DECISION IS DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-MADE. See the PER-FILE ROUTE DECISION section below. A dispatch that quietly defaults to one route for all files has not done the work this record asks for.

STANDING INSTRUCTION: re-verify every path, line number and hit count below against the tree before citing it again. They were measured at filing and they drift.

=== WHAT WAS MEASURED (2026-11-02, at HEAD 86b8fc759) ===

Pattern `FormalSystem|BimodalLogic|BimodalTools|ProofChecker|PlusLanguage`, counted over TRACKED files in the source store (`git ls-files agent-system/`). Hit counts are matching LINES, not occurrences.

The four substantive files:

- agent-system/extensions/formal/context/project/logic/domain/frame-constraint-landscape.md -- 37 hits. Line 5 states the coupling outright, verbatim: "Every Lean name below is fully qualified and lives in the ProofChecker (BimodalLogic) tree."
- agent-system/extensions/formal/context/project/logic/domain/ztime-no-finite-carrier-fmp.md -- 26 hits. The same coupling is stated at line 16: "qualified and lives in the ProofChecker (BimodalLogic) tree or in the named probe file."
- agent-system/extensions/lean/context/project/lean4/domain/sentence-translation-contract.md -- 17 hits. Hardcodes FormalSystem/SourceLanguage/Sentence.lean, BimodalTools/SentenceExport.lean and Tests/BimodalTest/ paths.
- agent-system/extensions/lean/context/project/lean4/domain/ladder-counter-observables.md -- 1 hit, at line 10, naming FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/LadderModel.lean. Likely a trivial de-specialization.

CONSEQUENCE: the formal and lean extensions ship these files to every consumer. A repository with no such Lean tree receives domain context whose named declarations and paths do not exist for it, and nothing currently detects this.

=== PER-FILE ROUTE DECISION -- NOT PRE-DECIDED, BY EXPLICIT RULING AT FILING ===

Two routes are on the table for each of the three substantive files. The implementer must choose PER FILE and record the grounds that settled it. The choice may legitimately differ per file.

ROUTE A -- RELOCATE. Move the file out of the shared store into the consuming repository's own per-repo context location, context/repo/, which is never overwritten by a deploy and is protected by that repository's .syncprotect (which already protects context/repo/project-overview.md). COST: whatever generic value the file carries for other Lean projects is lost to them.

ROUTE B -- DE-SPECIALIZE IN PLACE. Keep the file in the shared store, strip repository names and hardcoded paths, rewrite as generic guidance. COST: more work, and it risks discarding the concrete grounding that makes the file useful at all. A file whose every claim is a specific Lean declaration may not survive de-specialization as anything a reader can use.

Neither route is pre-selected and neither is the default. For frame-constraint-landscape.md and ztime-no-finite-carrier-fmp.md in particular, note that their own opening lines ANNOUNCE the coupling rather than hiding it -- weigh whether that is a file honestly declaring its scope (favouring Route A) or a fixable framing (favouring Route B).

=== TRIAGE INVENTORY -- THE FULL SWEEP, NOT JUST THE FOUR ===

The same sweep found 24 tracked files with at least one hit. The acceptance clause below is stated over the whole sweep, so the rest must be triaged, not ignored. Measured counts at filing:

EXPLICITLY LEGITIMATE, DO NOT TOUCH:
- agent-system/extensions/lean/scripts/tests/test-lean-src-roots.sh -- 11 hits. Lines 63-95 build a deliberate "BimodalLogic-shaped lakefile.toml" fixture (srcDir = "Tests" on one lib, several libs) and are correctly repo-named: the fixture's whole purpose is to exercise that shape.
- agent-system/extensions/core/context/reference/known-consumer-repos.json -- 2 hits, lines 18-19. A registry of consumer repositories; naming them is the file's function.

COSMETIC, DECIDE SEPARATELY WHETHER IT IS WORTH TOUCHING AT ALL:
- agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/plan-file-scope-harvest.sh -- 7 hits, including lines 85, 88, 309 and 325, which embed FormalSystem/, Tests/ and BimodalTools/ in explanatory comments only. No behavioral coupling: the script does not branch on these names.
- agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-plan-file-scope-harvest.sh -- 36 hits, the single largest count in the sweep. This is the harvest script's test, so its fixtures mirror those same comments; it is listed here rather than above only because its disposition follows whatever is decided for the script, and a 36-hit file should not be discovered unmentioned.

PLAUSIBLY LEGITIMATE, CONFIRM RATHER THAN ASSUME (spot-checked at filing; each looked like illustrative-example or provenance-comment use, which is the "consciously retained" class the acceptance clause allows):
- agent-system/extensions/literature/context/guides/literature-organization.md -- 8 hits, example filenames (Brastmckie_2024_BimodalLogic.pdf/.md) in a directory-layout illustration.
- agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/validate-state.sh -- 4 hits, lines 167, 1015, 1025 and 1032: measurement provenance in comments (where a historical count or a one-off repair was observed).
- agent-system/extensions/core/context/contracts/territory.md -- 2 hits, lines 66 and 70, an illustrative file_scope example.
- agent-system/extensions/typst/context/project/typst/standards/notation-conventions.md -- 1 hit, line 92, an illustrative repo-root-relative path.
- The remainder, each 1-4 hits: agent-system/extensions/literature/agents/literature-agent.md (4); agent-system/extensions/literature/context/project/literature/patterns/literature-rebuild-mode.md (3); agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (3); agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-batch-admit.sh (2); agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/mcp-server-ownership.md (2); agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md (2); agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-roadmap-generation.sh (1); agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh (1); agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/backfill-file-scope.sh (1); agent-system/extensions/core/context/guides/hard-mode-routing.md (1); agent-system/extensions/core/context/contracts/anti-analysis.md (1); agent-system/extensions/literature/scripts/literature-audit.sh (1).

=== NOT A BOUNDARY-VIOLATION RECORD -- VERIFIED CLEAN IN THE OTHER DIRECTION ===

This is pollution of the shared store by repo-specific CONTENT. It is NOT an instance of hand-authoring under a deploy tree. Verified at filing: diff -rq found byte-exact matches between the BimodalLogic deploy tree and the source store for .claude/context/project/lean4/, .claude/context/project/logic/, and all six deployed skill-lean-*/skill-lake-repair skills. There is no hand-authored local content under that repository's .claude/**. Do not re-frame this record as a source-store/deploy boundary violation.

=== DETECTION GAP -- RECORDED HERE, OWNED ELSEWHERE ===

Nothing currently catches repo-specific content entering the shared store. A second task for a detection gate was explicitly DECLINED at filing, so this record does not own one and must not grow one.

The adjacent open record is cross_repo_source_store_gate_blindness (numbered 401 in this task space at filing; re-resolve it by description rather than trusting the number). That record covers the cross-repo overlap/dependency gate being blind when two repositories file work against ONE shared store -- which is DUPLICATE-WORK detection, a different problem from content pollution. Any gate proposal belongs there, after that record's own owner-adjudication escalation is answered, and not as a third overlapping record.

=== DO NOT DUPLICATE -- EACH CHECKED AT FILING ===

- cross_repo_source_store_gate_blindness (401) -- cross-repo duplicate-work detection, as above.
- migrate_mis_sited_agent_system_tasks (390) -- owns moving mis-sited RECORDS into this task space. A data migration of task records, not of content.
- agent_system_task_siting_and_target_root (391) -- owns record siting and target-root resolution.

None of the three addresses repo-coupled CONTENT inside a shared store. NO DEPENDENCY EDGES were added to any of them, deliberately: they are adjacent, not blocking, and none of them has to land before this one can.

=== NOTE AT FILING -- DIRTY WORKING TREE ===

The source store's working tree was dirty at filing, including agent-system/extensions/lean/context/project/lean4/domain/ladder-counter-observables.md -- one of the four files above -- as well as agent-system/extensions/lean/manifest.json, agent-system/extensions/lean/index-entries.json, agent-system/extensions/lean/scripts/lean-challenge-snapshot.sh and two of its tests, plus agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lake-build-guard.sh and its test. Re-check that file's state before editing it; the 1-hit measurement above was taken against the working tree, not against HEAD.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

1. Each of the three substantive files (frame-constraint-landscape.md, ztime-no-finite-carrier-fmp.md, sentence-translation-contract.md) has a RECORDED route decision with the grounds that settled it, and has been relocated or de-specialized accordingly.
2. The 1-hit file (ladder-counter-observables.md) is resolved.
3. A grep for the five repo identifiers over tracked shared-store content returns only the self-labelled fixture, the consumer registry, and whatever comments were consciously retained -- each retention being a decision someone made, not a file that was never looked at.
4. The store is redeployed to a clean verify.

=== PROVENANCE ===

specs/reviews/review-2026-11-02.md in ~/Projects/BimodalLogic, High Priority Issues section. That review separately confirmed that BimodalLogic's own agent-system defects are already tracked by its frozen-record tracker, which is why this record belongs in the source store's task space and not in that repository's.

active_projects.title: Give lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --check a scope limit so a research prototype under specs/ stops forcing a false ambiguity failure
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: resolve `source_dir` from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one. Never hand-author under a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store (rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description, which lives under specs/**.

CROSS-REPO CITATION CAVEAT: the issue identifier cited below is an entry in a DIFFERENT repository's issue log -- BimodalLogic, at specs/849_forward_slack_discharge_and_exact_shift_iteration/issues.jsonl. The number 849 is a BimodalLogic task number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json; do not try to look it up here. This record is filed here, not in BimodalLogic, because an agent-system change belongs in the repository that owns the source store. Cross-repo overlap has no mechanical representation today; that gap is itself tracked by this repo's cross_repo_source_store_gate_blindness task.

CITATION: BimodalLogic:849:iss_1793754709802_bWVZnZ (class `tooling`, severity minor, implement phase).

=== THE DEFECT ===
`lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --check` has no scope limit, so a compiled research prototype parked under `specs/**` -- the sanctioned place for one -- forces a false ambiguity failure and exit 71 on a tree that is in fact correct.

=== ROOT CAUSE, RE-DERIVED BY DIRECT READ OF THE SOURCE STORE AT FILING (line numbers drift; re-derive before editing) ===
`do_check()` begins ~L198. It resolves each pinned identifier by walking the entire project root:
  - `find_lean_files(root)` (~L273-279) is `os.walk(root)` with `dirnames` filtered to exclude only the directory names ".git", ".lake" and "lake-packages".
  - The comparison loop (~L282-294) iterates that walk over `project_root` and skips exactly one further path, the pinned Challenge artifact itself (`challenge_abs`).
Any other `.lean` file anywhere in the tree is therefore a comparison target, including `specs/{NNN}_{slug}/prototype/*.lean`. When such a prototype declares a pinned name, `ambiguous` (~L297) is non-empty and the branch at ~L306-310 writes "ERROR: '{n}' resolves to more than one declaration in the current tree: {files}" and exits 71.

=== A SECOND ENUMERATION SITE -- DERIVED HERE, DO NOT FIX ONLY ONE ===
The R2 fallback path has its own independent enumeration and its own ambiguity hard-exit:
  - ~L602: `tree = git("ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", commit)`; ~L605: `lean_files = [p for p in tree.stdout.splitlines() if p.endswith(".lean")]`. That is every `.lean` path in the repo tree at that commit with NO exclusions at all -- not `.lake`, not the Challenge.
  - ~L652-660: `ambiguous` non-empty writes "ERROR: R2 fallback found more than one declaration named '{n}' at commit {commit[:12]}: {files}. Extraction ambiguity is a hard error, never a best-effort guess." and exits 71.
So a COMMITTED prototype under `specs/` reaches the same defect by the second path. If a scope notion is introduced, both sites should consume it rather than diverging; if only `--check` is fixed, the record must say why. The R2 site's "hard error, never a best-effort guess" stance is deliberate and must be preserved for genuine ambiguity.

=== MEASURED INCIDENT (carried from the originating repo's record; CARRIED-UNVERIFIED in this repository -- re-derive or re-cite at plan time) ===
Five of seven pinned names resolved to two declarations each: the landed declaration in `FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/LadderChain.lean` and the research prototype `specs/849_.../prototype/helpers-compiled.lean`. The implementer checked drift independently (whitespace-normalized header diff of all seven against Challenge.lean: MATCH 7/7) and did NOT edit the prototype, correctly treating it as the research record. The verdict is advisory by the script's own header, so nothing was blocked. The loss is that a mechanical check was silently replaced by a manual one.

=== DESIGN QUESTION -- DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-DECIDED ===
Candidate mechanisms, each with a real cost to weigh:
  (a) Exclude `specs/` in the enumeration. Cheapest, but hard-codes a repository-layout assumption and would also hide a genuine duplicate that some task legitimately parks under `specs/`.
  (b) An explicit `--scope` / `--include` flag. Pushes the decision out to every call site, and the call sites include a hook.
  (c) Read the task's own `file_scope`. Couples the script to state.json's `file_scope`, whose lifecycle is owned elsewhere in this repo (see the file-scope-lifecycle topic).
Research picks one and says why the others lose.

=== INVARIANT TO PRESERVE ===
Two declarations of a pinned name in the LIBRARY is a real finding and must remain a hard failure. The deliverable narrows WHERE the script looks, never WHETHER genuine ambiguity fails.

=== EXIT-CODE CAUTION ===
Prefer not to overload 71 further. This script's exit-code vocabulary is already being revised by the zero-goal task named in dependencies, which observes that 71 is documented as "Config error" in the script's own header while carrying several distinct conditions. Adopt whatever that task settles rather than inventing a parallel code.

=== DEPENDENCIES AND WHY (serialization against shared file territory, NOT absorption) ===
Both descriptions were read in full at filing; neither covers `--check`'s identifier resolution or its tree-walk scope, so this is a sibling record, not a duplicate.
  - `lean4_plan_with_zero_lean_goals`: same two lean files. Owns the exit-71 vocabulary for the EXTRACT step and the zero-theorem plan shape. A new scope mechanism must not reintroduce a 71 collision that task is in the middle of untangling.
  - `snapshot_lean_challenge_at_plan_time`: same two lean files plus the test suite. Owns WHEN the snapshot is invoked (moving it to plan time). Changing where `--check` looks while the invocation point is moving would land two uncoordinated edits in one script.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
(a) A `--check` run in a tree containing a `.lean` prototype under `specs/{NNN}_{slug}/` that declares a pinned name resolves to the library declaration and exits 0.
