active_projects.title: Emit deploy ordering in implement dispatch body
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system change request) of an /orchestrate batch over eight tasks (408, 464, 465, 466, 478, 489, 493, 495), session sess_1793993117_98582a. User-approved at the orchestrate-lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. SEVERITY: costly. All eight tasks in the batch reached [COMPLETED]; this defect caused no failure, it cost cycles.

## The defect

Implement-phase dispatch bodies carry no deploy-ordering instruction, so an implementation that edits the source store, redeploys, and then lands a further source edit leaves the deployed tree stale and is refused by the completion-deploy gate.

MEASURED: task 465 lost two full orchestration cycles. Its implement dispatch made source-store edits, redeployed via deploy-headless.sh, then landed a further source edit (a manifest.json registration) AFTER the deploy. orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's completion-deploy gate refused the completion write with exit 6 ("modified_files overlap agent-system/extensions/** and the deploy is stale") on two consecutive cycles, each deferring to the next cycle's Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint. The task reached [COMPLETED] only when the checkpoint's own post-deploy reconcile promoted it.

## The workaround that proved the fix

The orchestrate lead hand-patched a "DEPLOY ORDERING" paragraph into every subsequent implement dispatch prompt in the batch, and no later task hit the gate. That instruction belongs in the dispatch body orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh emits for every implement-phase dispatch, not in an ad-hoc addendum a human has to remember per dispatch.

## Scope

Add a deploy-ordering instruction to the implement-phase dispatch body emitted by agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh, stating that every source-store edit must precede the final deploy-headless.sh run and that no source-store edit may land after it. Cover the emitted instruction with a test in agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh.

## Constraints

- Emit the instruction for implement-phase dispatches only, not research or plan phases.
- Do NOT change the completion-deploy gate. The gate is correct; this task removes the cause of its firing, not the gate.

## Distinct from the already-adjudicated gate-side remedies

Verified by reading the records, not assumed. Three prior records attack the same cost from the gate/trigger/recovery side and leave the prevention side untouched:

- Task 442 (`deploy_before_implement_postflight_to_avoid_cycle_cost`, completed) evaluated a pre-postflight-sweep deploy trigger and deliberately left it UNBUILT, recording that decision in agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md. No gate logic or trigger predicate changed.
- Task 507 (`revisit_pre_sweep_deploy_trigger_ruling`, open) re-adjudicates that declined ruling against measured whole-cycle gate cost. Its file_scope is batch-orchestration-guardrails.md only.
- Task 367 (`reduce_deploy_staleness_completion_round_trip`, completed) widened the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint's post-deploy reconcile sweep so a refused task cannot stay invisible to the self-heal mechanism. The gate itself is unchanged.

This task acts on the PREVENTION side -- what the dispatch builder tells the implementing agent -- and touches none of those three files. It is complementary to task 507, not a substitute for it, and neither blocks the other.

## Durable evidence anchors

- issue-log entries: 465/iss_1794013002526_LmxN8I, 465/iss_1794013542296_YzqgQt
- refusing site: orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh completion-deploy gate, exit 6

## Visible hint override, recorded so a future reader can audit it

Both citing entries carried `suggested_channel: fix_now`. The orchestrate lead overrode that to the agent-system channel and said so to the user when seeking approval. The reason: there is no local code fix -- the durable remedy is a change to what the dispatch builder emits for every future implement dispatch.

## Overlapping open file territory

Task 487 (`identical_dispatch_halt_despite_phase_progress`, open) declares orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh in its file_scope, as do open tasks 360, 435, 449 and 450. No dependency edge is asserted here because none of them blocks this work; the overlap is recorded so batch admission orders rather than parallelizes them.

--- ADDENDUM (orchestration conclusion stage, 2026-11-10; purely additive, nothing above altered) ---
BLOCKING OBSTACLE MEASURED, not previously recorded here. test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh's
Group 18 (around lines 1395-1443) deliberately edits the plan file between two implement builds
(appending a phase heading) and asserts the two dispatch bodies hash EQUAL, on the stated premise
that the implement dispatch body is insensitive to plan-file content. Any change that emits
plan-derived or deploy-ordering content into the implement dispatch body makes the body
deliberately sensitive to exactly what that pin asserts it ignores, so this record's ask cannot
land without first amending Group 18 with fresh justification -- narrowing the existing pin to
mtime/size/sha/date-derived content and adding a companion pin for the NEW intended sensitivity --
rather than silently breaking it. Treat that amendment as its own phase, not a fold into the
emission edit. Evidence: issue-log entry iss_1794316250238_0MsPzs in
specs/487_identical_dispatch_halt_despite_phase_progress/issues.jsonl (recorded at plan time,
dispatch_seq 30). A sibling record reached the same wall independently and chose to reject the
in-body mechanism outright in favour of a persisted side-channel signal, for the stated reason
that correctness resting on a body line staying out of a hash strip pattern is drift-fragile;
weigh that precedent before committing to in-body emission here.

lint-agent-contracts.sh Check N completeness-net glob does not match the -implement-agent.md naming variant.

Check N (Net 1/Net 2) enumerates the agents its completeness net must cover with the glob '*implementation*agent.md'. That pattern does not match the '*-implement-agent.md' variant, so epi-implement-agent.md and founder-implement-agent.md fall outside the net entirely. One consequence is already observable: CHECK_G_EXCLUDED_RELATIVE_PATHS lists epi-implement-agent.md, but because the glob never reaches that file, the exclusion entry is dead code that can never fire.

Found mechanically while redesigning Check J as fail-closed, and deliberately left unfixed there because it falls outside that work's declared file_scope.

Deciding between widening the glob, sourcing Net 1/Net 2 from enumerate_dispatchable_agents(), and normalising the agent filename convention is the substance of this task. Prefer the enumerate_dispatchable_agents() route if it holds up: the Check J fix established that sourcing a check's universe from a filename glob is itself the trap, and Check J now iterates that function directly.

CHANNEL: /orchestrate conclusion channel (c), follow-up task, session sess_1793993117_98582a.
CITATIONS: {task 478, iss_1793993679918_nAiaZ8}, class COVERAGE_GAP, severity minor.

BACKLOG RECONCILIATION: three open records name lint-agent-contracts.sh in their own file_scope (audit_cross_extension_bounded_wait_duplication, durable_record_for_gate_enforced_verbatim_fragments, rebase_bounded_wait_guidance_on_180s_ceiling), but all three concern bounded-wait prose and verbatim-fragment enforcement, not Check N's enumeration source. No intent overlap, so no dependency edge is asserted. Every duplicate-of-open verdict the audit returned for this proposal carries shared_paths null and mechanical_class none, i.e. semantic threshold noise rather than real territory overlap.

Report and summary heading skeletons are nonconformant across fifteen agents beyond the four already remediated.

A mechanical sweep against validate-artifact.sh's own REPORT_SECTIONS and SUMMARY_SECTIONS lists, using the validator's own regex, found heading-contract gaps well beyond the four formal research agents whose conformance work produced this finding:

CONFIRMED FAIL, summary skeleton missing Impacts, Follow-ups and References:
  agent-system/extensions/nix/agents/nix-implementation-agent.md
  agent-system/extensions/nvim/agents/neovim-implementation-agent.md
  agent-system/extensions/web/agents/web-implementation-agent.md
CONFIRMED FAIL, report skeleton missing Context and Scope:
  agent-system/extensions/web/agents/web-research-agent.md
DOMAIN-SHAPED, larger pre-existing cluster (ten founder, three present, two epidemiology agents): skeletons use domain-customised headings such as Summary in place of Executive Summary, yet still write into specs report directories subject to the generic check.
NO SKELETON AT ALL: seven agents across typst, z3, books, latex, python, rust and cslib carry neither an embedded report skeleton nor a pointer to the canonical contract.

The authoritative enumeration is specs/495_formal_research_agents_report_section_conformance/fixtures/sweep-baseline.txt, produced and re-run by the formal-agent conformance work. It is explicitly authoritative over that work's own research report, which undercounted the founder-extension list (the sweep found ten founder agents failing; the report described eight while listing nine).

The canonical required-heading contract now lives once in report-format.md and summary-format.md, with general-research-agent.md and the four formal agents pointing at it rather than carrying their own copies. That pointer-not-copy pattern is the template to follow here; do not reintroduce per-agent verbatim copies.

Decide per cluster rather than uniformly: the four confirmed FAILs are straightforward remediation, while the domain-shaped cluster needs a ruling on whether a domain-customised skeleton should conform to the generic contract or whether the validator should recognise a declared domain shape. Resolve that ruling before editing fifteen files.

CHANNEL: /orchestrate conclusion channel (c), follow-up task, session sess_1793993117_98582a.
CITATIONS: {task 495, iss_1793997449338_BjRvG0} class artifact-format-gap, and {task 495, iss_1794018627494_M2yr6l} class measurement discrepancy.

The shared paths are a coarse footprint match, not intent overlap, so no dependency edge is asserted here. If the two are ever dispatched concurrently, batch admission's own file_scope overlap check will serialize them. Every other duplicate-of-open verdict carries shared_paths null and mechanical_class none, i.e. semantic threshold noise.

active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation, session sess_1794023900_f4ac5a. User-approved at the lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only.

CITATION: #418:iss_1794024837652_7HqnmR. The entry carried no suggested_channel hint; routing it to the agent-system channel is the orchestrator's own classification, on the grounds that the defect is in a lint this system owns rather than in any task's work product. Severity: recurring minor -- a workaround exists and nothing is blocked, but it fired three separate times inside a single migration phase, each time costing a diagnosis pass.

PROVENANCE: every file, line number, and quoted string below was re-derived by direct read of the source store at creation time (2026-11-06), not copied from the cited entry. Line numbers move -- re-derive before editing.

LIVE SYMPTOM. Gate 27's MISSING_DECLARATION check reports a violation against a suite that is in fact fully compliant, whenever a header comment or explanatory prose in that suite names the resolver helper by its literal identifier without an equal number of mentions of the declarer helper. Observed three times inside one migration phase, on scripts/tests/test-force-phases.sh, scripts/tests/test-lint-json-channel-discipline.sh, and scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh.

ROOT CAUSE, VERIFIED AGAINST THE SCRIPT. scripts/lint/lint-subject-resolution-declaration.sh's classify_file(), around lines 232-239:

    resolve_subject_count="$(grep -c 'common_test_resolve_subject' "$f" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    declare_subject_count="$(grep -c 'common_test_declare_subject' "$f" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    ...
    if [[ "$resolve_subject_count" -gt "$declare_subject_count" ]]; then
        hits="$hits MISSING_DECLARATION"
    fi

Both figures are whole-file, unanchored `grep -c` SUBSTRING counts over every line of the file -- comments, heredoc bodies, and string literals included, with no call-shape anchoring and no comment stripping. Any line that names the resolver identifier without also naming the declarer identifier adds one to the resolve side only, and a single such line is enough to make a compliant file count resolve > declare.

LATENT FRAGILITY, VERIFIED LIVE -- cited because it shows the trap is not confined to the three files already reworded. scripts/tests/test-dispatch-metrics.sh has four genuine common_test_resolve_subject call sites (lines 47, 51, 55, 59) and four genuine common_test_declare_subject call sites (lines 50, 54, 58, 62), yet the lint counts 5 and 5 -- balanced only because its line 43 comment happens to name BOTH identifiers on one line. Had that comment named only the resolver, which is the natural phrasing for explaining why lib/common.sh is sourced, the file would count 5 against 4 and the lint would flag a suite that is entirely correct. The same accidental balance holds in scripts/tests/test-common-lib.sh, test-lint-test-harness-adoption.sh, and test-validate-state.sh, each of which also carries a comment mentioning the identifiers.

THE WORKAROUND IN PLACE IS THE DEFECT BEING REPORTED. The fix applied at the time was to reword prose so it says "the shared resolve-subject helper" rather than naming the function. Five suites now carry such de-identified prose: test-force-phases.sh (lines 25, 50, 90), test-lint-json-channel-discipline.sh (line 18), test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh (line 9, hyphenated as "resolve-subject-helper"), test-orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh (line 68), and test-reconcile-demote-stranded.sh (line 33). The cited entry attributes three of these to this workaround; the other two may predate it for unrelated reasons, so re-derive the set by grep rather than trusting this enumeration. Either way the standing cost is the same: the next author who writes the identifier in a comment, which is the natural thing to do, trips a gate for no reason.

SCOPE -- rule on the counting predicate explicitly and record the reasoning. Candidate directions, offered as starting points and NOT as a prescription:
  (1) Strip comment lines before counting. Cheap and closes the observed cases, but a heredoc-embedded fixture or a string literal naming the identifier still counts.
  (2) Anchor on a call-shaped pattern (the identifier at a command or command-substitution position, followed by whitespace or a quote) rather than a bare substring. This closes the heredoc and string-literal cases too.
  (3) Both: count only lines that are neither comments nor inside a quoted fixture body AND that match a call shape.
Whichever is chosen, the KNOWN LIMITATION header block (around lines 42-51) MUST be rewritten to state what the new predicate can and cannot see. It currently claims file-level regex matching as its precedent and names the limitations that follow from that; it must not keep claiming a limitation it no longer has, nor quietly retain one it still does.

DO NOT RE-LITIGATE any of the following -- they are settled and out of scope: the three bad shapes themselves (HAND_DUP, INLINE_LOOP, UNMIGRATED_IMPLICIT_ORDER); the Layer-2 file allowlist mechanism and its existing permanent entries; the deliberately narrow scripts/tests/ scan corpus and the documented reason it does not use lint_corpus_scan_collect_files's shared-corpus path; and the mandatory-declaration contract itself. Only check 3's counting predicate is in question.

VERIFICATION OBLIGATION.
  - scripts/tests/test-lint-subject-resolution-declaration.sh Case 3 (around lines 110-133) already seeds a genuine missing-declaration file and asserts a non-zero exit whose message names the seeded file. That case MUST stay green: the fix must not blind the check to the real defect it exists to catch.
  - Add a new case that is RED before the fix and GREEN after: a fully compliant suite whose comment names the resolver identifier without naming the declarer. This is the regression anchor for the false positive.
  - Gate 27 in scripts/verify-deploy.sh (around line 1980) runs this lint with --verbose over the source store and must stay green.
  - Restoring the de-identified prose in the five suites above to name the identifier directly is the natural end-to-end confirmation, and is what actually removes the standing trap for the next author. Decide whether to do that here or to leave it as follow-up, and say which.

DOCUMENTATION. context/standards/shell-script-testing.md (around lines 153-168) states the mandatory-declaration contract and describes this lint as detecting "a common_test_resolve_subject call with no paired common_test_declare_subject". That description is currently aspirational rather than accurate -- the implementation counts mentions, not calls. If the predicate becomes call-shaped, the description becomes true as written; if it stays count-based, the doc must say so plainly. Either way the doc must not leave a reader believing comments are exempt from the count when they are not.

DEPENDENCY RATIONALE (file territory, not a sequencing preference). Task 448 declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lint/ and agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/ as whole directories in its file_scope, plus context/standards/shell-script-testing.md -- every file this record edits falls inside that declaration. This repository runs concurrent writers in one shared working tree, so an unordered overlap is sequenced by a dependency edge rather than left to chance.

PRIOR ART -- DISPOSED OF EXPLICITLY AT CREATION TIME, DO NOT REDISCOVER OR RE-LITIGATE.
  - Task 418 (completed) is this record's parent. It created this lint, the explicit common_test_resolve_subject/common_test_declare_subject pair, the mandatory-declaration contract, and Gate 27 itself -- and it applied the prose-rewording workaround described above. The defect reported here is in what that work shipped, not a gap it left unexplored. The relationship is parent_task, not duplication.
  - Task 448 (open) declares scripts/lint/ and scripts/tests/ as whole directories plus context/standards/shell-script-testing.md. Its subject is containing a test harness's deliberate-break mutation of the shared source store -- a different defect in overlapping territory. Sequenced here by dependency edge; nothing in its scope is re-litigated.
  - Task 445 (open) and task 511 (open) both declare context/standards/shell-script-testing.md. 445 is the Gate 8 expected-versus-new failure distinction; 511 is an enumeration grep sweeping a gitignored venv. Both are documentation-only overlaps on one shared file and are deliberately left unsequenced rather than chained, to avoid over-constraining the backlog.
  - Task 435 (open) declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ and agent-system/extensions/core/context/ as whole directories, for a repo-wide per-class prose reword of three deleted lifecycle command names. That declaration overlaps essentially every agent-system record and is deliberately left unsequenced on the same grounds the rest of the backlog leaves it unsequenced.
  - The creation-time backlog audit returned a cluster of roughly 0.5-scored duplicate-of-open and covered-by-closed verdicts carrying mechanical_class=none against unrelated records. Those are uncorroborated Pass-2 shortlist entries, inflated by this description's length -- the exact condition task 491 (open) exists to fix. They were checked, not accepted, and are not evidence of duplication.

active_projects.title: Rule on a staged-vs-working-tree divergence signal for a pathspec commit, and name the partial-stage trap in the staging-scope standard
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**. ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation, session sess_1794023900_f4ac5a. User-approved at the lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. CITATIONS: #418:iss_1794001639995_QvyIy9 (the near-miss itself, severity costly); #418:iss_1794001112756_1CPE72 (the partial-stage attempt and its motivation); #418:iss_1794001757595_GJUSiy (a live concurrent sibling writer observed in the same working tree during the same dispatch); #418:iss_1793989293251_3pfJ9z (a plan-time territory collision with a concurrent sibling over a shared file). None of the four carried a suggested_channel hint; routing them to the agent-system channel is the orchestrator's own classification, on the grounds that the hazard lives in shared commit tooling and its governing standard. Severity of the primary entry: costly. PROVENANCE: every file, line number, and quoted string below was re-derived by direct read of the source store at creation time (2026-11-06), not copied from the cited entries. Line numbers move -- re-derive before editing. The incident narrative itself is CARRIED-UNVERIFIED from the cited entries; the mechanism it turns on was independently re-confirmed against the script, as recorded below. LIVE SYMPTOM. A hand-built partial patch was staged with `git apply --cached` against agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json, specifically so that one task's own two hunks would be committed and a concurrent sibling's uncommitted lib/gate-store-fixture-lib.sh provides.scripts line would be left untouched. The subsequent `git commit -- ` nevertheless committed the WORKING-TREE content for that path, sweeping the sibling's unrelated uncommitted line into the commit. It was caught immediately via `git show --stat` and corrected with a second narrow commit removing that line from HEAD, after which the sibling's line was restored into the working tree uncommitted so their in-progress work survived exactly as found. No work was lost. The report is the near-miss and the standing unsoundness, not a live breakage. ROOT CAUSE IS KNOWN GIT SEMANTICS, ALREADY DOCUMENTED IN THE SCRIPT. scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh's header carries a dedicated block (the "Git semantics discovered empirically while diagnosing V8" note, around lines 259-270) stating that `git commit -- ` RE-READS the current working-tree content fresh for each named path AT COMMIT TIME and does not commit whatever `git add` most recently staged. The index is therefore not the authority for a pathspec commit, and any partial stage of a named path is discarded by the commit that follows. The defect is not that this is unknown; it is that nothing refuses, warns about, or documents the partial-stage idiom that the semantics silently defeat. WHY NO EXISTING GATE CATCHES IT -- VERIFIED, AND THE CRUX TO RULE ON. The V8 post-commit integrity gate (header around lines 164-207; implementation around lines 780-828) takes its PRE-COMMIT INTENT SNAPSHOT as `git hash-object -- "$v8_f"` of each enumerated path's WORKING-TREE content, with an explicit "absent" sentinel when the file is not on disk. V8's operative definition of intent IS therefore the working tree. In the cited incident the working tree held the sibling's line, the commit landed exactly that content, and V8 compared a MATCH -- correctly, by its own contract. V8 structurally cannot see index-vs-working-tree divergence because it never reads the index. The V7 verification loop does read the index, but only for PRESENCE of a path, never for its content. So no gate in the script notices that the caller staged a subset and git committed the superset, and the script exits 0 with nothing printed. THE QUESTION TO RULE ON, NOT A PRESCRIPTION. A defensible outcome here is option (2) -- no code change, documentation only. Do not assume a code change is required. (1) Add a PRE-COMMIT divergence check inside git-commit-scoped.sh: for each surviving positive pathspec, compare the staged content against the working-tree content (per-file index blob vs. `git hash-object`, or `git diff --cached --name-only --

` against `git diff --name-only --

`) and REFUSE, or WARN, when they differ. Refusal is the stronger posture but will also fire on the ordinary and entirely legitimate case of a file edited further after it was staged; decide whether that case is a real population in this pipeline or only an artifact of hand workflows, and record the evidence for whichever answer is given. (2) Change nothing in the script and treat sub-file partial staging as simply UNSUPPORTED, documented as such -- the script's contract then being stated plainly as "for every named path you get the working tree as it stands at commit time". (3) A narrower middle: detect only the specific shape where the index holds a STRICT SUBSET of the working-tree changes for a named path (the partial-stage signature) and warn on that alone, leaving a plain edited-after-staging file unflagged. Options (1) and (3) both interact with V8: if a pre-commit divergence signal exists, V8's own snapshot choice becomes a deliberate, stated decision rather than an unexamined one, and the header must then say which authority each gate consults and why they differ. DOCUMENTATION OBLIGATION, INDEPENDENT OF WHICH OPTION WINS. context/standards/git-staging-scope.md's "Concurrency Qualifier: Targeted Staging Is Necessary But Not Sufficient" section (around lines 223-258) states that "Path granularity is the file -- an explicit-path `git add` cannot subdivide a file by author", then routes the reader to the two sanctioned remedies (the first-claim contended-path lease inside git-commit-scoped.sh, and per-dispatch working-tree isolation). It does NOT name the partial-stage attempt anywhere. A reader who has just been told that granularity is the file will reach for `git apply --cached` as the obvious sub-file workaround, and that reach is silently unsound under `git commit -- `. The section MUST name the trap explicitly: sub-file staging does not survive a pathspec commit, so it is not an available remedy, and the lease and tree isolation remain the only sanctioned ones. WHY THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The same dispatch separately observed a concurrent sibling editing scripts/verify-deploy.sh live, mid-dispatch, in the same working tree (#418:iss_1794001757595_GJUSiy), and a plan-time territory collision with a concurrent sibling over a shared file (#418:iss_1793989293251_3pfJ9z). Concurrent writers in one shared working tree are this repository's normal operating condition, not an exceptional state, which is precisely what makes a silently-unsound narrowing idiom worth closing or naming. DO NOT RE-LITIGATE any of the following: V5's contended-path lease and its first-claim posture; V8's existence, its working-tree snapshot being valuable on its own mechanism-agnostic terms, or its dedicated exit code 5; the prohibition on a bare `git commit`; the settled bare-directory-pathspec policy and its lint. Note also that the incident's own commit was a HAND-RUN `git commit --`, not a git-commit-scoped.sh invocation, so "the script was not involved" is a point for the planner to weigh, not a reason to close the record -- the standard it governs is read by the humans and agents who run git by hand. DEPENDENCY RATIONALE (file territory, not a sequencing preference). Three open records already declare scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh and scripts/tests/test-git-commit-scoped.sh in their file_scope: task 461 (the V7 refusal of a positive directory pathspec for a `git rm --cached` untracking), whose declared three-file scope is identical to this record's; task 484 (collapsing per-path scope-excursion issue rows); and task 501 (cycle-postflight containment predicate parity). Because this repository runs concurrent writers in one shared working tree -- the very hazard this record reports -- the overlap is sequenced by dependency edges rather than left unordered. Tasks 430, 446 and 486 additionally declare context/standards/git-staging-scope.md but none of the two scripts; that overlap is documentation-only and is deliberately left unsequenced rather than chained, to avoid over-constraining the backlog. PRIOR ART -- DISPOSED OF EXPLICITLY AT CREATION TIME, DO NOT REDISCOVER OR RE-LITIGATE. - Task 374 (completed) is the closest prior art and shares this record's exact three-file scope: it diagnosed and fixed the silent staging drop in git-commit-scoped.sh, and its product IS the V8 gate. It does NOT cover this case, and that distinction is the whole substance of this record. V8's intent authority is the WORKING TREE (`git hash-object` of each enumerated path), so it catches a divergence arising BETWEEN its snapshot and the commit -- a concurrent writer changing the file after staging -- and compares a correct MATCH when the index held a narrower subset than the working tree all along. Read that record's outcome before planning, then state in the plan which authority each gate consults and why. - Task 461 (open) declares a scope identical to this record's three files, for a different defect: the V7 refusal of a positive directory pathspec for a `git rm --cached` untracking whose content is still on disk. Sequenced here by dependency edge. - Task 484 (open) and task 501 (open) both declare git-commit-scoped.sh and its suite -- 484 collapsing per-path scope-excursion issue rows, 501 giving the cycle-postflight containment site predicate parity. Both sequenced by dependency edge for file territory, not for any logical ordering between the subjects. - Tasks 430, 446 and 486 (all open) declare context/standards/git-staging-scope.md but neither script. Documentation-only overlap on one shared file, deliberately left unsequenced. - Task 435 (open) declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ and agent-system/extensions/core/context/ as whole directories for a repo-wide prose reword; that declaration overlaps essentially every agent-system record and is left unsequenced on the same grounds the rest of the backlog leaves it unsequenced. - Closed and settled -- do not reopen: task 302 (the scoped-commit directory pathspec and first-claim task lease), task 199 (the concurrent-dispatch isolation posture decision record, which context/standards/git-staging-scope.md already cites as the home of both sanctioned remedies), task 277 (an unresolvable pathspec made a hard error), task 304 (an out-of-repository pathspec aborting the whole commit, V9), task 226 (staged deletions dropped by the V2 gate). - The creation-time backlog audit returned a cluster of roughly 0.4-to-0.5-scored duplicate-of-open and covered-by-closed verdicts carrying mechanical_class=none against unrelated records. Those are uncorroborated Pass-2 shortlist entries, inflated by this description's length -- the exact condition task 491 (open) exists to fix. They were checked, not accepted. - Task 448 (open) declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/ as a whole directory, which covers this record's test suite but neither of its other two files. Its subject -- containing a test harness's deliberate-break mutation of the shared source store -- is unrelated to this one. A single-file overlap inside a broad directory declaration, deliberately left unsequenced: the dependency edges above already serialize this record against every open task that names git-commit-scoped.sh itself.

active_projects.title: Repair the always-failing extensions-directory fallback in the task-type detection suite
active_projects.description:
Repair the always-failing extensions-directory fallback in the task-type detection suite

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/**; both are permitted in this description.

--- MEASURED EVIDENCE ---

scripts/tests/test-task-type-detect.sh resolves its real-manifest root in two branches. The first detects the source-store shape directly and is correct. The second -- the fallback, reached whenever the first does not match, which is precisely when the suite runs from the DEPLOYED copy -- cannot ever succeed:

    REAL_EXT_ROOT="$(common_test_resolve_candidate "real extensions directory" \
      "$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)/extensions")" || exit 2

common_test_resolve_candidate (scripts/lib/common.sh) selects the first candidate satisfying
[ -f "$_common_candidate" ]. The single candidate passed here is an extensions DIRECTORY, so the
[ -f ] test fails against it unconditionally, the helper falls through to its own not-found error,
and the suite exits 2 before reaching the real-manifest case the variable exists to serve.

Confirmed structurally: the helper's loop body tests [ -f ] and nothing else; the candidate path
ends in a directory component by construction. Confirmed historically: this branch is byte-identical
before and after the subject-resolution migration that surfaced it, so the migration neither caused
nor touched it. The branch was deliberately left on the older candidate helper by that migration's
own plan, which is why the mismatch survived.

--- THE CONSEQUENCE ---

Gate 8 runs the deployed copy, which is exactly the shape that takes the failing branch. The
real-manifest case guarded by REAL_EXT_ROOT -- the one asserting a bare "literature" mention no
longer force-routes to meta -- therefore never runs under Gate 8. This is a silent coverage hole,
not merely a red suite: the assertion that regression test exists to make is not being made.

--- REQUIRED DIRECTION ---

Resolve a DIRECTORY with a directory-appropriate test rather than passing one to a file-only
helper. Research must settle which of these the tree's own conventions favour, with evidence
rather than preference:

- A directory-mode selector on the shared helper, if one already exists or if other callers need it.
- A plain inline [ -d ] check in this suite, if this is the only site that resolves a directory.

Prefer whichever option leaves exactly one home for the behaviour. If the shared helper gains a
directory mode, research must enumerate every existing common_test_resolve_candidate call site and
confirm none of them silently changes meaning.

Research must also settle whether other suites pass a directory to this file-only helper. A single
grep over the call sites answers it, and an unfixed sibling would be the same silent hole.

--- VERIFICATION ---

- A fixture proving the fallback branch resolves the real extensions directory when it is taken --
  exercised by running the suite from the DEPLOYED copy, which is the shape that takes it. A fixture
  that only ever runs the source-store shape cannot reach the branch under repair and does not count
  as evidence.
- A fixture proving the first branch still wins when the source-store shape matches, so the repair
  does not silently reroute the source-store path through the fallback.
- The real-manifest assertion (bare "literature" no longer force-routes to meta) is observed actually
  executing under the deployed shape, not merely not-failing. A skipped assertion and a passing one
  are indistinguishable in the suite's current output, which is how this hole stayed open.
- Final phase declares the complete gate set with an explicit source-store TARGET (the bare form
  silently skips the source-store-only gates).

Known-unrelated pre-existing failures: Gate 3 lean4 doc-lint missing index.json entry; Gate 20
eager-load budget over baseline; Gate 22 shellcheck SC2155 in the lean extension's
lean-plan-compliance-check.sh; Gate 24 two /ide references in the memory extension's docs; Gate 8
suites test-detect-noop-bash.sh, test-four-tier-conflict.sh, test-guard-git-push.sh. Do not
attribute these to this work and do not fix them here.
--- AUDIT DISPOSITION (mechanically corroborated overlaps, each disposed of rather than inherited) ---

The proposal audit returned two mechanically corroborated overlaps against open records. Both are
coarse-declaration artifacts, not genuine duplicates, and neither owns the defect above:

- Record 435 (reword_dead_lifecycle_command_prose_per_class), verdict subset-of-open, shared paths
  scripts/lib/common.sh and scripts/tests/test-task-type-detect.sh. That record's file_scope declares
  whole DIRECTORIES (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ among roughly eighty entries), so it
  mechanically contains every file under them. Its subject is rewording prose that names three deleted
  lifecycle commands, per site and per class. It does not touch candidate resolution, directory-versus-file
  tests, or REAL_EXT_ROOT. The overlap is an artifact of directory-level declaration.

- Record 448 (contain_deliberate_break_source_mutations), verdict duplicate-of-open, shared path
  scripts/tests/test-task-type-detect.sh. That record likewise declares scripts/tests/ as a directory.
  Its subject is containing a regression-anchor source-store mutation so a concurrent session cannot
  observe or inherit it. That is a test-isolation concern about deliberate mutation; this record is a
  resolution-helper type mismatch. Disjoint mechanisms.

Both records were open and not_started at this record's creation. If either is dispatched concurrently
with this one, the shared file is scripts/tests/test-task-type-detect.sh and the two must be serialized
rather than run in parallel; add a dependencies[] edge at that point rather than widening either scope.

ORIGIN: /orchestrate conclusion stage, channel (c) follow-up task.
CITATION: {task 418, iss_1794028461910_9Z5Zqz}, class "test-resolution-quirk". That entry recorded the
defect as one of several pre-existing failures observed but deliberately not fixed in its own dispatch.
The entry carried no suggested_channel; channel (c) was chosen because the repair needs its own research
into the shared helper's call sites rather than an inline patch.

active_projects.description:
Add purpose-written `.title` fields to specs/state.json's active_projects entries so TODO.md stops rendering truncated description prose as task names.

CONTEXT: the entry schema (project_number, project_name, status, task_type, description, topic, dependencies, created, last_updated, file_scope) has no title field populated — all 61 entries lack `.title`. This is NOT a defect. `.title` is an optional field with a documented fallback chain: `generate-todo.sh:188` ("Title fallback: derive from project_name if title is empty", `title="${project_name//_/ }"`) and `generate-task-order.sh:192` ("(.title // .description // .project_name) -- a purpose-written .title is preferred over the top of a long prose .description; .description remains the fallback for title-less tasks, and .project_name is the last resort when both are absent"). The cost of relying on the fallback is readability: TODO.md currently renders the first ~60 characters of `description`, so entries read like "720 — RE-SCOPED 2026-10-03: THIS TASK IS THE CITATION RE-POINT..." and "709 — STANDING (second re-scope; SUPERSEDES BOTH..." — truncated status notes rather than names.

SCOPE: (1) write a concise noun-phrase `.title` for each entry in specs/state.json's active_projects, deriving it from `description` and `project_name`; target under 70 characters, no dates, no status prefixes such as RE-SCOPED/STANDING/HARD/CAPSTONE, no task-number references; prioritize the dependency-ready wave-1 set (127, 128, 178, 257, 298, 464, 481, 502, 559, 566, 570, 604, 616, 617, 664, 709, 711, 712, 713, 714, 716, 720, 722, 723, 725, 726, 728) since those are the entries selected from next. (2) Regenerate TODO.md through the existing generator and confirm the titles render in both the grouped-by-topic listing and the dependency-wave table. (3) Verify the fallback path still works for any entry deliberately left title-less, so the optional-field contract is preserved rather than silently becoming mandatory.

NON-GOALS: no schema change (the field is already supported by both generators); no edit to `description`, `project_name`, `topic`, or any other existing field; no change to the generators themselves; no renaming of task directories, whose names derive from `project_name` and must stay stable.

Effort: small-to-medium, mostly editorial judgment rather than code.

active_projects.description:
Evaluate whether the formal:logic implement-phase routing should resolve to a Lean-capable agent when the plan touches .lean files.

EVIDENCE. The formal extension's manifest declares, explicitly and not as a fallback, `routing_agents.implement["formal:logic"] = "general-implementation-agent"` (confirmed by `command-route-agent.sh implement formal:logic`, which resolves `via=noncore-exact`). The task_type `formal:logic` therefore never reaches `lean-implementation-agent`, which the lean extension reserves for `lean4`, `lean4:lake` and `lean4:version`. A formal:logic task whose work is substantially Lean runs without the lean-lsp MCP path, the Lean-specific implementation contracts, and the lake build guidance that a lean4-typed task receives.

OBSERVED CASE. A completed formal:logic task ran its implement phase under general-implementation-agent across seven files, four of them requiring new Lean theorems in `FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/PlusWitnessFamily/Incompleteness.lean`, a `#print axioms` baseline probe in `scripts/check-module-invariants.sh`, scoped and full `lake build` runs, and `lake build BimodalTest`. It completed successfully, so this is a potential improvement rather than a defect report — but it did the Lean work without Lean tooling.

FRAME THIS AS AN EVALUATION, NOT A PREDETERMINED CHANGE. `formal:logic` legitimately covers modal-logic research, proof theory and Kripke-semantics work that touches no Lean at all; the research phase already routes it to `logic-research-agent` rather than `lean-research-agent` for exactly that reason. A blanket reroute of the implement phase to `lean-implementation-agent` would therefore be wrong for part of the population. The question to answer is whether routing should become conditional on the plan's harvested `file_scope` containing `.lean` paths, and if so, where that conditional belongs: in the manifest schema (which today maps task_type to agent name with no predicate), in `command-route-agent.sh`, or in the orchestrator's dispatch composition.

SCOPE. (1) Determine how many non-terminal and recently-completed formal / formal:logic / formal:math / formal:physics tasks declare or harvest `.lean` paths in file_scope, to size the affected population rather than generalizing from one case. (2) Decide among: leave as is and document the rationale; reroute formal:logic wholesale; or introduce a file_scope-conditional routing predicate. (3) If a conditional is chosen, specify where it lives and what it does when file_scope is absent (29 non-terminal tasks currently have no file_scope key at all, so the predicate must have a defined behavior for the unknown case, and must not silently pick the heavier agent on no evidence). (4) Apply the resulting decision in the SOURCE STORE (`~/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/formal/manifest.json` or the routing library), never by hand-patching the deployed `.claude/` tree, then redeploy via `deploy-headless.sh`.

NON-GOALS: no change to research-phase or plan-phase routing, both of which are working as intended; no change to the lean extension's own `lean4*` routing; no new agent definitions.

active_projects.description:
Land the three agent-system context extensions recorded by the cslib omega-automata survey

WHY THIS EXISTS. The cslib omega-automata survey (task 736, completed) closed with an operator hand-off list of six findings it deliberately did not act on, stating in its own summary: "This task spawns no follow-on tasks of its own; filing any of these is the operator's call." Five of the six are now discharged or owned: (a) the falsified `Nat.nth` note in FormalSystem/ForMathlib/Combinatorics/InfiniteRamseyPairs.lean was corrected by task 711 (the module now reads "available in this project's..."); (b) the two stale statements in specs/ROADMAP.md's E3 section are gone; (d) the Hodkinson-Reynolds Handbook sections are owned by task 734; (e) "port nothing, treat cslib as a read-only reference" is settled and relitigates nothing; (f) the 736 file_scope drift is descriptive and was flagged rather than fixed by design. Item (c) -- three context-extension recommendations -- was NEVER FILED. Verified 2026-10-08 against every non-terminal meta and markdown record (729, 730, 731, 738): none covers any of the three. This task is that filing.

THE EDIT TARGET IS THE SOURCE STORE, NOT `.claude/**`. `.claude/` here is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact; a hand-authored file landing there is silently wiped by the next regeneration. Resolved 2026-10-08 from .claude-extensions.json: the source store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/<name>/`, and each deployed path mirrors a path under it. Re-resolve before editing rather than trusting this note. Task 736 recorded `.claude/` as STALE for `core filetypes lean typst` at its own dispatch; a 2026-10-08 orchestration re-observed STALE for `core` and `typst`. Remedy is `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh`, never a hand-patch of a deployed file, which would mask the divergence instead of fixing it.

WHAT IS OWED, three items, each independently completable. A partial outcome (two landed, one recorded as declined with a reason) is complete and valid.

(1) `proof_wanted` AS A TRUST SURFACE DISTINCT FROM `sorry`, in the lean extension's metadata-trust-surfaces.md. Source file verified present at `lean/context/project/lean4/domain/metadata-trust-surfaces.md`. The substance, from 736's own Decisions section item 1: a `sorry`-grep returned 0 across all 54 surveyed cslib files while 8 main theorems were unproved, because `proof_wanted` emits NO declaration at all -- so `#print axioms` on such a name returns "unknown constant" rather than a `sorryAx` line, and both the grep and the axiom probe read as clean. 736 logged this as a `false-negative-verification` issue at severity `costly`. The document already catalogues what Lean metadata rows are NOT checked by; this adds the `proof_wanted` row to that catalogue. State the detection method that does work (a `proof_wanted` census per file) alongside the two that do not.

(2) A NEW `external-library-port-assessment.md` PATTERN. Verified absent from the entire source store 2026-10-08; the name implies `lean/context/project/lean4/patterns/`, which exists. The content is 736's own assessment method, which produced a defensible "port nothing" verdict and should be reusable rather than re-derived: toolchain and Mathlib-pin distance as the first gate (76 commits apart was the decisive figure); a `proof_wanted`/`sorry` census of the candidate declarations before treating any as a resource; fork-versus-upstream divergence (the local fork was 155 commits behind, and several files the consuming description listed as upstream were absent from it); the cost of a Lake `require` edge stated as a concrete consequence for the consuming tree rather than as a preference; and the read-only-reference verdict as the default. Record the dissent-and-rejection shape too: 736 reported the dependency alternative the dispatch invited, and rejected it on a stated ground, rather than silently omitting it.

(3) A STEM-COLLISION PASS FOR THE LITERATURE AUDIT. Candidate hosts verified 2026-10-08 under `literature/scripts/`: literature-audit.sh, literature-fidelity-audit.sh, literature-combining-audit.sh; choose by reading them, do not assume. The substance: ids must be matched WHOLE against the global index, never by author-year stem. 736 ran this pass by hand over one sub-index and found THREE unrecorded collisions -- `piterman_2007` (two directories for apparently one paper, divergent fidelity, one `verified_conversion` and one unset); `vardi_1996` (`vardi_1996_automata_ltl` `verified_conversion` versus `vardi_1996_automata-theoretic-ltl` `no_source_pdf`, OPPOSITE fidelity verdicts, and the pre-existing entry carried no hazard); and `vardi_wolper_1986` (file-level versus directory-level records in the same directory, both `verified_conversion`, no fidelity divergence but not interchangeable). The pre-existing `thomas_1997` / `thomas_1997_languages_automata` hazard is the precedent the pass generalizes: one stem, two papers, one of them `no_source_pdf`. A hand pass finding three unrecorded instances in one sub-index is the argument for mechanizing it.

CONSTRAINTS. No Lean, no proofs, no edits under FormalSystem/ or Tests/. Make no claim about cslib's mathematical correctness: the deliverable is agent-system context about how to ASSESS such a library, not a verdict on one. Do not relitigate the "port nothing" recommendation -- it is settled and item (2) documents the method that reached it, not the question. Do not weaken the identity-hazard convention to make a mechanized pass easier; if whole-id matching cannot be mechanized without loosening it, record that as the finding and leave the pass unimplemented. Each of the three items is in a DIFFERENT extension (lean, lean, literature), so expect three separate source-store trees and do not collapse them into one file.

ACCEPTANCE. For each of the three: either the content landed in the named source-store file (new or extended), the deployed tree regenerated via deploy-headless.sh so the deployed copy matches, and a one-line record of what was added; or a recorded reason for declining it, naming what made it not worth doing. Mixed outcomes across the three are expected. The acceptance signal is that the source store, not `.claude/**`, carries every edit -- a change visible only in the deployed tree has not landed.

SCOPE. Source-store files under /home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/{lean,literature}/ plus the regenerated deployed copies. SET file_scope AT PLAN TIME, after reading the three candidate literature-audit scripts to decide which hosts the pass. Do not edit specs/archive/** and do not edit task 736's records: they are the historical source being acted on.

**`roadmap-integration.sh --regenerate` IS SILENTLY INOPERATIVE ON THIS ROADMAP.** Verified live: `bash .claude/scripts/roadmap-integration.sh --regenerate` exits 1 with ZERO stdout and ZERO stderr and writes nothing, because `specs/ROADMAP.md` carries none of the headings the assembler needs — it is a Stage-based authored document, not the `## Open work` / `## Next` generated layout the script expects. Pick one and land it: either teach the script the Stage-based layout, or decide that `specs/ROADMAP.md` is AUTHORED-ONLY and make `--regenerate` say so LOUDLY (a named error on stderr and a documented exit code) instead of aborting in silence. active_projects.title: lake-build-guard replays stale result for env lean FILE
active_projects.description:
Stop `lake-build-guard.sh` from replaying a stale shared result when the verified unit is a single file passed through to `env lean`.

OBSERVED LIVE, NOT HYPOTHESIZED. `bash .claude/scripts/lake-build-guard.sh build -- env lean FILE` REPLAYED the previous invocation's captured output -- errors citing line numbers of the OLD contents of FILE -- after FILE had been rewritten at the same path. The run was worked around with `--no-share`. The staleness fingerprint evidently does not cover an arbitrary file argument forwarded to `env lean`.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE ITEM IN ITS BATCH. A guard that silently replays a stale result undermines EVERY single-file verification in the system, including verifications later cited as evidence in reports, summaries and gate decisions. A stale green replay is indistinguishable from a fresh green run to the caller unless the caller inspects stderr for the `lake-build-guard: REPLAY:` marker -- the script's own usage text says exactly this under `--no-share`. The failure mode is silent acceptance of an obsolete result, not a crash, so nothing downstream flags it.

WHERE TO LOOK -- RE-DERIVE RATHER THAN TRUST; the following is a snapshot of a ~1242-line script. `collect_fingerprint_files()` documents itself as listing every `*.lean` source under the project tree. `compute_fingerprint()` defaults to `stat` mode (file METADATA), with content hashing available only opt-in via `LAKE_BUILD_GUARD_FINGERPRINT=hash`; the header notes hash mode exists specifically to close a gap stat mode leaves open. `compute_scope_key()` keys sharing on scope, and `decide_sharing()` gates the replay. The header's own list of known limitations ALREADY concedes that a caller "cannot distinguish a replay from a fresh run without passing --no-share". `LAKE_SUBCOMMANDS` includes `env` and `lean`, so an `env lean FILE` invocation passes the subcommand allowlist unremarked.

DISCRIMINATE BETWEEN TWO CANDIDATE MECHANISMS BEFORE FIXING ANYTHING -- they have different remedies and only measurement settles which occurred. (i) The rewritten FILE is not a member of the fingerprinted set at all -- it lies outside the collected root, or outside the `*.lean` glob -- so rewriting it CANNOT move the fingerprint, and no amount of strengthening the hash helps. (ii) FILE is in the set, but stat-mode metadata did not change discernibly between the two runs, in which case content hashing for named file arguments is sufficient. Reproduce the replay mechanically first; do not infer the mechanism from the header's prose.

DECIDE AND LAND ONE OF TWO. The originating request names both and they are NOT equivalent. (a) Extend the fingerprint and/or the scope key to cover the explicit file arguments of the forwarded command, so an `env lean FILE` invocation's shareability tracks FILE's own content. (b) Refuse to share a result for an `env lean ...` invocation at all -- treat it as implicitly `--no-share`. Option (b) is strictly safer and much cheaper to reason about, at the cost of giving up sharing for a real use case. Option (a) preserves sharing but must be shown correct for a file lying OUTSIDE the fingerprinted tree, which is the harder case and the one mechanism (i) above describes. If (a) is chosen, prefer content hashing over stat metadata for explicitly named file arguments regardless of the ambient `LAKE_BUILD_GUARD_FINGERPRINT` mode: stat-mode equality is the weaker predicate and this is precisely where it failed.

ACCEPTANCE -- A FAILING-FIRST REGRESSION TEST IN `tests/test-lake-build-guard.sh`, WHICH ALREADY EXISTS AND MUST BE EXTENDED RATHER THAN REPLACED. The test must: (1) run `build -- env lean FILE`; (2) rewrite FILE at the SAME path so its compile outcome changes; (3) re-run the identical command WITHOUT `--no-share`; (4) assert the second run reports the NEW outcome. Demonstrate the test fails against the unmodified script before landing the fix. Additionally, the script's documented STALENESS POLICY -- the numbered conditions in its header, which include "the record's POST-build fingerprint equals the WAITER's CURRENT fingerprint" and "a missing or empty recorded scope_key is treated as NOT shareable (fail closed)" -- MUST end up agreeing in writing with whatever behavior is landed. The acceptance condition for the documentation half is that a reader of the header alone can predict the file-argument case.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. `.claude/**` is a gitignored, regenerated deploy artifact; a hand edit there is wiped by the next deploy and will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. Resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` for the owning extension (`core`, whose source store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`) and edit at the mirroring path there, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`. Then redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`. The `.claude/**` paths in file_scope are declared only so the admission overlap gate can see the collision surface; they are NOT the edit target.

The originating issue-log entry is in `specs/760_ladder_model_cell_stabilization_lemma/issues.jsonl`, entry_id `iss_1791710205724_8rTs68` (the change request also referenced it as `iss_1791711671927_8rTs68`), severity minor, class "tooling bug or gap", resolution worked_around, hinted channel `agent_system` (hint not overridden).

This defect was re-observed independently during orchestration of the ladder-realization-theorem record and approved at the orchestrate-lead level through the conclusion stage's agent-system change-request channel. The citation is recorded here rather than filed as a duplicate record because this record already owns the defect and already carries both candidate remedies. Entry: `specs/761_ladder_realization_theorem/issues.jsonl`, entry_id `iss_1792362861192_o99zDu` (class `tooling-trap`, severity `costly`, phase `implement`).

NOTHING IN THIS RECORD'S SCOPE, REMEDY SET OR ACCEPTANCE CONDITIONS CHANGES. The second observation matches the account above in every structural respect: a repeated `build -- env lean <same path>` invocation replayed the previous run's captured output after the file at that path had been corrected on disk, and the run was worked around with `--no-share`. Two things it adds are worth carrying into the fix.

  (1) A MECHANISM CLAIM BEARING ON THE (i)/(ii) DISCRIMINATION ABOVE, WHICH IT DOES NOT SETTLE. The second observation reports that the `scope_key` is the lake ARGUMENT VECTOR and that the project inputs were unchanged between the two runs. That is consistent with candidate mechanism (i) -- the rewritten file is not a member of the fingerprinted set at all -- and inconsistent with (ii). It is NOT a measurement of set membership; it is an inference from reading the script, which is exactly what this record already forbids relying on ("Reproduce the replay mechanically first; do not infer the mechanism from the header's prose"). Treat it as a prior that makes (i) the first hypothesis to test, never as the finding itself.

active_projects.title: postflight writes detail-free blocking issue entry on partial returns
active_projects.description:
Stop the orchestrate postflight from writing a detail-free blocking issue-log entry on every blocker-bearing partial return, and settle that entry's classification.

ROOT CAUSE IS A TYPE MISMATCH, MEASURED NOT HYPOTHESIZED -- THE DETAIL WAS AVAILABLE AND WAS THROWN AWAY. In `scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh`, the `partial)` arm of the dispatch-status case statement builds the issue narrative with `partial_blockers_detail=$(echo "${handoff:-null}" | jq -r '(.blockers // []) | join("; ")' 2>/dev/null)`, then substitutes a literal fallback string when that comes back empty. The handoff's `blockers[]` is an array of OBJECTS, not strings: `scripts/validate-handoff.sh` requires each entry to carry `phase` and `target` (it counts an entry lacking them as an invalid blocker), and the live returns carry `{phase, target, verbatim_goal, what_was_tried, why_it_failed}`. `jq`'s `join` on an array of objects does not degrade -- it ERRORS (`string ("") and object ... cannot be added`, exit 5). The `2>/dev/null` swallows the error, the command substitution yields the empty string, the `-z` guard fires, and the literal fallback text is what gets recorded. Re-derive this before fixing: run the `join("; ")` expression against a blocker-bearing `.return-meta.json` WITHOUT `2>/dev/null` and read the jq error directly. Note the arm is only reachable when the blocker count is already greater than zero, so the fallback branch as written is reachable ONLY through this error path -- a non-empty array that joins to an empty string is otherwise impossible. That makes the fallback string a permanent output, not a rare degradation.

WHAT THE LOST DETAIL ACTUALLY WAS, AND WHY THE LOSS MATTERS MORE THAN THE NOISE. The discarded `blockers[]` objects carried the refuted goal statement verbatim, what had been tried, and why it failed -- several paragraphs of exactly the content the log exists to preserve. `context/formats/issue-log.md`'s surface-relation table states the MIRROR obligation this call site is implementing: the handoff keeps naming blockers for the immediate successor dispatch, but because `.orchestrator-handoff.json` is overwritten on every dispatch, a `blockers[]` entry about to be written should ALSO be recorded via `issue-record.sh` so the detail survives the overwrite. The call site's own in-code comment cites that obligation by name. The obligation is therefore currently discharged in form and defeated in substance: the entry exists, the detail it was supposed to rescue is gone, and the handoff that held it has since been overwritten. This half of the record is the high-value half and is wholly independent of the classification question below -- land it first.

THE TEST SUITE PASSES OVER THE DEFECT. `scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh` already has a regression case for a blocker-bearing partial, and it already uses object-shaped blockers (`target`, `verbatim_goal`, `why_it_failed`). It asserts only the state.json status transition and the aux signal -- never the recorded `what_happened` text -- so the suite is green while the narrative is empty. ACCEPTANCE for the detail half: extend that existing case (do not replace it) to assert that the recorded `issues.jsonl` entry's `what_happened` contains content drawn from the blocker objects, and show the assertion fails against the unmodified script. Decide explicitly how an object is rendered into one prose paragraph -- which subfields are included, in what order, and what happens when an optional subfield is absent -- rather than leaving the format implicit in a jq expression. Removing the `2>/dev/null` on this particular substitution, or otherwise surfacing a jq failure here instead of silently substituting, is in scope: a swallowed error is what converted a fixable bug into an invisible one.

CLASSIFICATION: THREE SEPARABLE QUESTIONS, ONLY ONE OF WHICH THE ORIGINATING REQUEST SETTLED. (1) CLASS. The call site hard-codes `--class "environment"`, whose admission test in `issue-log.md`'s seed-class table is "the local or CI environment (missing binary, version mismatch, permissions) caused the cost". A blocker-bearing partial is almost never that -- in the originating run the blocker was a refuted mathematical statement. The class is wrong for the general case, and it is hard-coded where the actual class is not knowable from the postflight's vantage point; evaluate whether a less specific but honest class, or a class derived from the handoff, is the right remedy. (2) SEVERITY. The call site hard-codes `--severity blocking`. Unlike the class, this appears DEFENSIBLE against the four-rung scale in `issue-log.md`'s "Severity Scale": `blocking` is admitted when "work could not proceed at all ... the dispatch stalled or had to hand off because of it", which is precisely a blocker-bearing partial. Do not reclassify severity merely to reduce channel volume -- if the entry is genuinely blocking, suppressing it by downgrading severity hides a real signal. Argue the severity question on the admission test, and record the argument. (3) VOLUME. The same unresolved blocker is re-recorded on every subsequent partial dispatch: the originating task carries two entries with byte-identical `what_happened`, differing only in `entry_id`, `timestamp`, `dispatch_seq` and `session_id`. Even with full detail restored, N dispatches against one unresolved blocker yield N near-duplicate blocking entries. Consider de-duplication keyed on blocker identity rather than on dispatch.

THE SUPPRESSION IDEA HAS AN ORDERING OBSTACLE -- CHECK IT BEFORE COSTING IT. The originating request asks to consider suppressing the entry entirely when the partial outcome already carries a `user_decision` payload that was relayed and answered. In the current script the `user_decision` relay is a LATER work block (its own section, several hundred lines below the `partial)` arm), so at the moment the issue is written the relay has not yet run. Suppression therefore requires reading `user_decision` off the handoff early, or deferring the issue write until after the relay -- not a one-line guard. Also decide what "answered" means mechanically: `return-metadata-file.md` documents `user_decision` as producer-owned and relayed-never-resolved, so the presence of the payload does not by itself establish that the user answered. If no mechanical test for "answered" exists, say so and scope the suppression to the weaker, checkable condition or drop it with that reason recorded.

DO NOT ENCROACH ON THE CONCLUSION-STAGE FILTER PREDICATE. Whether a reclassified entry still reaches a channel is governed by `context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Filter Predicate" (an entry enters classification only when `resolution` is `open` or `worked_around`). A separate record -- the one covering null-resolution entries being dropped by the conclusion stage -- owns that predicate, `scripts/issue-record.sh`, and `context/formats/issue-log.md`. This record MUST confine its edits to this call site's own arguments and the postflight script plus its test, leaving the predicate, the writer script, and the format document to that record. If that record has already landed a predicate change by the time this one is implemented, read the predicate as it then stands and honor it. If a prose amendment to `issue-log.md` is judged genuinely necessary, add a serializing dependency edge at that point (`update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add`) rather than editing a file another record claims -- the file_scope declared here is deliberately disjoint from it for exactly this reason.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. `.claude/**` is a gitignored, regenerated deploy artifact; a hand edit there is wiped by the next deploy and will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. Resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` for the owning extension (`core`, whose source store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`) and edit at the mirroring path there, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`. Then redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`. The `.claude/**` path in file_scope is declared only so the admission overlap gate can see the collision surface; it is NOT the edit target.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. Cite durable anchors -- file names, function names, section headings, field names, flag names -- only.

The originating issue-log entries are in `specs/760_ladder_model_cell_stabilization_lemma/issues.jsonl`, entry_ids `iss_1791711671927_JbPqvi` (dispatch_seq 3) and `iss_1791716590257_0MGDRu` (dispatch_seq 6); both severity `blocking`, class `environment`, resolution `open`.
