active_projects.title: Name the typst-sync gate as the cause when git-commit-scoped.sh reports a refused commit
active_projects.description:
META TASK. ONE defect, ONE record: when `git-commit-scoped.sh`'s commit attempt is refused by
this repository's typst-sync pre-commit gate, the script's own caller-facing verdict misnames the
cause as the V8 silent-staging-drop defect and calls the refusal "non-blocking", naming neither
the gate that refused nor the remedy that clears it. The deliverable is the DIAGNOSTIC MESSAGE
ONLY.

EDIT TARGET, binding. Per `rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md` this repository's `.claude/`
tree is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from a source store; a hand-authored
file landing under `.claude/**` is silently wiped by the next regeneration -- the edit appears to
succeed and has no lasting effect. Make every edit under the source store at the path mirroring
the deployed `.claude/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh`. RE-DERIVE the store rather than trusting
this note, but know what re-derivation currently yields: `source_dir` lives PER-EXTENSION at
`.extensions.<name>.source_dir` in `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json`, not as a top-level
key. A top-level `jq -r '.source_dir'` returns null and must NOT be read as the key being
absent. Re-derive with:

  jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json

which currently yields `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`, so the edit
target is `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh`. The owning extension is
`core`, not `typst` and not `lean`: the file to change is the commit wrapper, not the gate. If
`source_dir` is absent or its path does not exist when this task runs, record that as an
observation of its own rather than silently hand-authoring under `.claude/**`.

=== THE DEFECT AS OBSERVED ===

MEASURED {task 838, entry_id iss_1793728724405_1fBgOG} (class `gate collision`, severity
`costly`, resolution open). A commit touching `FormalSystem/**/*.lean` is refused by the
typst-sync pre-commit gate unless the same commit also carries a regenerated
`typst/generated/status.typ`, whose theorem and line counts are derived from the Lean tree.
`git-commit-scoped.sh` surfaced this as a "PARTIAL commit" report rather than naming the gate as
the cause.

COST, which is why this is filed rather than absorbed. It recurred at EVERY phase of that
implementation run, and each recurrence cost a diagnosis cycle -- the operator had to re-derive
the same cause from the same misleading text repeatedly. One recurrence additionally provoked a
reproduction probe that committed `README.md` under the placeholder message `x` (commit
`947dd9e8d`); the amend that would have folded it into the phase commit was refused by the
history-rewrite guard because a concurrent writer was live, so that commit remains in history.
That stray commit is a consequence of the misdiagnosis, not a separate defect, and it is NOT in
scope here: do not attempt to rewrite history to remove it.

THE REMEDY THAT ACTUALLY WORKED, each time, and the text the new message must carry:

  bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix
  # then add typst/generated/status.typ to the commit pathspec

=== MECHANISM -- VERIFIED BY SOURCE READING, NOT YET REPRODUCED END-TO-END ===

The following is a reading of the deployed script at the time this record was written. Confirm it
against the source store before acting, and confirm the end-to-end shape by actually driving a
refusal; the claims below are code-path reasoning plus the measured symptom, not a reproduction.

(1) `commit_output=$(git commit -m "$full_message" -- "${pathspecs[@]}" 2>&1)` captures the
    hook's stderr, and `echo "$commit_output"` later emits it on STDOUT. The gate's own text is
    therefore present but buried mid-stream, below the script's own authoritative-sounding
    stderr lines.

(2) The V8 post-commit integrity gate runs UNCONDITIONALLY, regardless of `commit_exit` -- its
    own header comment says so. When the hook refuses, no commit is created, so every
    V8-snapshotted path compares as `absent from HEAD` (or as differing content), V8's mismatch
    array is non-empty, and it prints on stderr: "ERROR: git-commit-scoped.sh detected a PARTIAL
    commit -- one or more named positive pathspecs did not land in HEAD as intended (Verified
    Finding V8). This is the silent-staging-drop defect: ...". That attribution is WRONG for this
    shape. Nothing was silently dropped; a gate refused the whole commit.

(3) `if [ "$commit_exit" -ne 0 ]; then echo "NOTE: Nothing to commit or git commit failed
    (non-blocking)" >&2; fi` then characterizes a HARD gate refusal as non-blocking, which
    invites exactly the wrong response -- proceeding as though nothing is owed.

(4) THE EXIT CODE IS ALREADY CORRECT AND MUST NOT CHANGE. V8's dedicated `exit 5` is guarded by
    `[ "$commit_exit" -eq 0 ]`, so it does NOT fire on a refusal; the script falls through to
    `exit "$commit_exit"`, which is git's own nonzero code. The defect is PURELY TEXTUAL. A fix
    that alters exit codes has exceeded its scope.

WHERE THE GATE LIVES, as durable anchors the new message may name. `core.hooksPath` is
`.githooks`, so the gate is `.githooks/pre-commit`; it invokes
`scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --counts-only`, fires only when the staged set touches a `.lean`
path, and is blocking rather than auto-regenerating. Its own text already names the remedy
(`lake build && bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix && git add typst/generated/status.typ`).
The gate is NOT broken and must not be edited by this task -- the hook's diagnosis is correct; it
is the wrapper's verdict on top of it that is wrong.

=== THE DESIGN QUESTION TO SETTLE, NOT A PARSER TO PATCH ===

`git-commit-scoped.sh` is deployed into repositories that do not have a typst gate, so the fix
must NOT hard-code one repository's hook. Research must settle which of these the change is, and
say why:

  (a) Detect the refusal class generically -- a nonzero `commit_exit` whose `commit_output`
      indicates a pre-commit hook refusal rather than an empty diff -- and reframe BOTH the V8
      ERROR and the "non-blocking" NOTE for that shape, re-emitting the hook's own captured text
      as the authoritative cause instead of burying it. This generalizes to every hook in every
      deploy and names no repository-specific path in the script.
  (b) Additionally pattern-match the typst-sync gate specifically to name `--fix` and the
      `status.typ` pathspec in the wrapper's own words.

(a) is the structurally sound half and is likely sufficient on its own, since the hook already
prints the remedy and (a) promotes that text rather than paraphrasing it. Prefer (a); adopt (b)
only if research shows the hook's text does not in fact reach the caller, and if it does, keep
any repository-specific knowledge out of the script body. The minimum acceptable outcome is that
a reader of the script's output can tell a gate refusal from a staging drop WITHOUT re-reading
the script.

=== TERRITORY -- WHY THIS DEPENDS ON THE CONTINGENCY/CONTAINMENT RECORD ===

Open record #839 (`plan_contingency_file_scope_and_containment_drop`, not_started) already claims
`agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh` AND
`agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-git-commit-scoped.sh` in its `file_scope` --
both of this record's files. The two changes are INDEPENDENT in substance: #839 settles the V10
containment guard and the `plan-file-scope-harvest.sh` contract, which is a different code path
from the post-commit reporting block changed here. Neither subsumes the other and neither should
be closed as a duplicate of the other.

They are nonetheless the same file with no mechanism to serialize them, which `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s
batching guardrail names as a reason to sequence rather than exclude. The edge runs #839 -> this
record, with #839 first, because #839 is the structural change that may itself move the reporting
block this record edits, and because #839 must settle a design question before its own code lands.
Applying the smaller message change on top of the settled structure is strictly cheaper than the
reverse. If #839 is abandoned or descoped away from `git-commit-scoped.sh`, this record becomes
independent and the edge may be dropped.

=== SCOPE BOUNDARY -- THREE THINGS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED ===

(1) THE PLAN-AUTHORING HALF IS ALREADY OWNED ELSEWHERE. Open record #785
    (`lean_plan_gate_collision_authoring_guidance`, not_started) owns the gate-collision facts a
    Lean implementation plan must anticipate BEFORE a criterion is written -- including this
    exact typst-sync surface, its `--fix` remedy, and the pre-commit-versus-later-verification
    asymmetry. Its `file_scope` is entirely within the lean extension and does not overlap this
    record. DO NOT write plan-authoring guidance here and DO NOT duplicate #785. It is named as
    related context only: a reader who wants "how should a plan have avoided this" goes there,
    while this record answers only "what should the script have said when it happened".

(2) The stray `947dd9e8d` commit and the history-rewrite guard refusal described above are
    consequences, not deliverables. No history rewrite.

(3) Two further findings from the same run were considered for this channel and DELIBERATELY
    EXCLUDED by the user's choice. They are NOT in scope and no task is to be created for them:
    the Scope-Hypothesis inventory-consumer miscount, and the non-importable prototype file under
    `specs/**`.

=== DELIVERABLE HYGIENE ===

Every edited file lies outside `specs/**`, so its contents -- including any new message string --
must carry no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and
no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). The
script names (`typst-sync-check.sh`, `git-commit-scoped.sh`), the flag spellings
(`--counts-only`, `--fix`), the generated path `typst/generated/status.typ`, the hook path
`.githooks/pre-commit` and the existing finding labels (V6, V8, V10) are durable anchors and may
be cited freely. The originating task number, the issue entry_id, the adjacent record numbers
above and the `947dd9e8d` sha may NOT appear in the script or in any deliverable prose -- they
live in this record only.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

(1) A pre-commit-hook refusal no longer produces the V8 "PARTIAL commit ... silent-staging-drop
    defect" ERROR as its cause attribution, and the V8 ERROR still fires unchanged for the shape
    it genuinely owns (a commit that WAS created and still dropped a named path).
(2) The "non-blocking" characterization no longer applies to a hard gate refusal.
(3) The hook's own text reaches the caller as the authoritative cause, not buried below the
    script's own stderr lines.
(4) The remedy is recoverable from the output without re-reading the script.
(5) No exit code changes: a hook refusal still exits with git's own nonzero code via
    `exit "$commit_exit"`, and the dedicated codes 4/5/6/7 keep their existing guards and
    precedence.
(6) No repository-specific hook knowledge is hard-coded into the script, or if any is, the
    research record states why (a) alone was insufficient.
(7) `scripts/tests/test-git-commit-scoped.sh` covers the refusal shape, asserting on the new text

(8) The typst gate itself (`.githooks/pre-commit`, `scripts/typst-sync-check.sh`,
    `typst/generated/status.typ`) is unmodified.
(9) `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` reports `RESULT=landed_verify_clean` afterwards.

active_projects.description:
OBSERVED 13 times during task 846's implementation. Every `agent-system/extensions/core/**` path was dropped from its phase-commit pathspec by `git-commit-phase.sh`, each reported with the message text `not contained in this task's declared file_scope` (git-commit-phase.sh, the `--what-happened` string at the excursion-report call site). Citations, all from task 846's `issues.jsonl`: iss_1793736794251_k7Q3J8, iss_1793736794311_yUp8Vp, iss_1793737815724_0ZfGnJ, iss_1793737815788_QHk1wn, iss_1793737815847_SJ3yxu, iss_1793737815907_UKDkzX, iss_1793737815965_izbdkL, iss_1793737816029_P1dXET, iss_1793737816087_3YZSsX, iss_1793738678082_9E2Jin, iss_1793738678146_o1Q504, iss_1793741189717_sYrKgg, iss_1793741189826_eDqokf.

TWO COMPOUNDING CAUSES. The task must address both or state explicitly why not.

(1) This repository's source store is EXTERNAL. `jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json` resolves to `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core` -- a different git repository. A path there is not under this repo's root at all, so a containment check against this repo's `file_scope` cannot match it, and a commit in this repo could not carry it even if the check passed. Independently confirmed: `agent-system/` does not exist in this repository at all, so even the plain `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/...` entries present in task 846's `file_scope` match nothing locally.

(2) The declared `file_scope` carried LITERAL, UNEXPANDED `$SD/...` entries. Verify this directly rather than trusting this description: `jq -r '.active_projects[] | select(.project_number==846) | .file_scope[]' specs/state.json` shows `$SD/manifest.json`, `$SD/scripts/state-write.sh`, `$SD/scripts/validate-state.sh`, `$SD/scripts/lib/project-number-inuse.sh`, `$SD/scripts/tests/test-validate-state.sh`, `$SD/scripts/test-state-write-concurrency.sh`, and `$SD/context/reference/state-management-schema.md`. Those strings match nothing mechanically. No `SD=` assignment exists in `git-commit-phase.sh` or `update-task-status.sh`, so the variable is not expanded anywhere on the commit path. ESTABLISH WHERE THE UNEXPANDED FORM IS INTRODUCED before proposing a fix -- candidate sites are a plan's Files-to-modify list, a postflight `--file-scope-add` call (the flag is consumed by `orchestrator-postflight.sh`, `command-gate-out.sh`, `update-task-status.sh`, `reconcile-task-status.sh`, `skill-base.sh`, and `backfill-file-scope.sh`), or the planner's own authoring.

WHY IT MATTERS, STATED HONESTLY. No work was lost this time: the dispatched agent noticed and committed the source store separately, and all six files are confirmed committed there across four commits. The defect is that nothing ENSURED that. An agent that did not notice would have left the deliverable uncommitted in the source store while this repo's phase commit reported success. The excursion notice is indistinguishable from the ordinary, correct refusals the guard emits when it is genuinely preventing over-staging. The guard is not malfunctioning -- it is correctly declining to stage paths outside the repo. What is missing is a sanctioned route for the external-source-store case.

DESIGN SPACE, all acceptable, decide with evidence. (a) Teach `file_scope` to express a source-store path in a form that resolves -- expanding `source_dir` at the point the scope is declared, or adopting an explicit marker the containment check understands. active_projects.title: Fix validate-handoff.sh crash-as-false-negative and settle the canonical blockers shape
active_projects.description:
META TASK. Fix a validator that reports a well-formed handoff as invalid, and settle the
canonical `blockers` shape that three different authorities currently disagree about.

=== MEASURED SYMPTOM, RE-DERIVABLE ===

During cycle 2 postflight of the ladder-realization work, `orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh` ran
`validate-handoff.sh` against that task's `.orchestrator-handoff.json`. The validator printed
eleven consecutive `[PASS]` lines and not one `[FAIL]`, then postflight emitted:
  ERROR: HANDOFF VALIDATION FAILED - <file> fails validate-handoff.sh's required-field checks
Reproduce (read-only):
  bash .claude/scripts/validate-handoff.sh specs/761_ladder_realization_theorem/.orchestrator-handoff.json; echo "EXIT=$?"
Observed: EXIT=5, and the output STOPS after "Blockers array present with 3 entry(s)" - the
"All blockers have required fields" line, the Validation Summary block, and the final verdict
line are all absent. The validator never reaches its own summary.

=== ROOT CAUSE, PINNED - NOT A HYPOTHESIS ===

`validate-handoff.sh` sets `set -euo pipefail`. Its Check 7 block, having confirmed a non-empty
`blockers` array, loops over the entries probing each as an OBJECT:
  has_phase=$(jq -r ".blockers[$i].phase // \"__MISSING__\"" "$HANDOFF_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
In the observed handoff the `blockers` entries are STRINGS, not objects. Indexing a string with
`.phase` is a jq runtime error ("Cannot index string with ..."), jq exits 5, `2>/dev/null`
discards the message, and under `set -e` the failed command substitution terminates the script
immediately with that exit 5. Confirm the per-entry failure directly:
  jq -r '.blockers[0].phase' specs/761_ladder_realization_theorem/.orchestrator-handoff.json; echo "EXIT=$?"
Note that 5 is not a documented exit code: the script's own header documents only 0 (valid),
1 (invalid) and 3 (file not found). The script therefore has an undocumented crash exit that is
indistinguishable, to any caller testing `-ne 0`, from a legitimate validation failure.

=== WHY THE CONSEQUENCE IS WORSE THAN A WRONG MESSAGE ===

The postflight call site treats any non-zero exit as a required-field failure, then tries to name
the failing fields by parsing `^\[FAIL\]` lines out of the captured output. A crash produces no
FAIL lines, so that parse yields an empty list and the `--extra-detail-json` flag is omitted by
the call site's own never-guess rule. The result is a HANDOFF_VALIDATION_FAILED system defect
raised against a handoff that is in fact well-formed, carrying no evidence of what failed,
because nothing did. A defect channel that reports healthy inputs as defective erodes trust in
every other entry it carries; this one firing is enough to warrant the fix.

=== THE REAL DISAGREEMENT: WHAT SHAPE IS `blockers`? ===

Settle this FIRST; it decides which side of the fix is the non-conforming one. Three authorities
disagree, measured:
  (a) `context/schemas/orchestrator-handoff-schema.json` - `blockers.items` is `type: "object"`
      with `required: ["phase", "target"]`, plus optional `verbatim_goal`, `what_was_tried`,
      `why_it_failed`. Its own description calls this "Canonical wrap-up/hard-mode blocker shape".
  (b) `extensions/lean/agents/lean-implementation-hard-agent.md` - instructs, in prose: "On
      `partial` or `blocked`: populate `blockers` with verbatim goal text from plan checklist."
      Followed literally, that yields an array of STRINGS, which is what the live handoff holds.
  (c) `validate-handoff.sh` Check 7 - probes `.phase`/`.target` unguarded, i.e. assumes (a) and
      crashes rather than failing on (b).
So the writer's instruction and the schema contradict each other, and the validator cannot survive
the contradiction. Do not resolve this by guarding the validator alone: that would leave a writer
producing data its own schema rejects, silently. Decide which shape is canonical, then conform the
other two sides to it, and say in the plan which authority was chosen and why.

A fourth data point to weigh, because it cuts against (b): the open record
`postflight_detail_free_blocking_partial_issue_entry` (task 770) asserts as measured fact that
"the live returns carry `{phase, target, verbatim_goal, what_was_tried, why_it_failed}`" and that
jq's `join` on them errors. Both that record and this one observed a jq exit 5 on `blockers`, from
OPPOSITE shape assumptions - which means the shape varies across writers or across time. Establish
the actual distribution before ruling; a ruling that explains only one of the two observations is
incomplete. Check the object-shaped and string-shaped producers separately rather than assuming one
global shape.

=== STRUCTURAL HARDENING, IN SCOPE ===

Independently of the shape ruling: an unguarded `jq` under `set -euo pipefail` with `2>/dev/null`
converts any data-shape surprise into a silent, undocumented, non-zero exit with no diagnostic.
Make the validator detect a shape it cannot probe and report it as a real `[FAIL]` line with a
documented exit code, so the summary block is always reached and callers can distinguish
"invalid handoff" from "validator crashed". Removing or redirecting the error-swallowing
`2>/dev/null` on these probes is in scope and is the reason this was invisible.

=== TERRITORY - DO NOT TAKE THESE FILES ===

`orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh` is claimed by three open records (tasks 770, 823 and 842) and
`system-defect-record.sh` by task 842. This record deliberately declares NEITHER, and confines
itself to the validator, the schema and the lean hard agent's instruction. If the fix turns out to
require changing how the call site interprets the validator's exit status - a reasonable outcome,
since distinguishing crash from failure is only useful if the caller acts on it - add a dependency
edge with `update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add` rather than editing a file another record owns.
Recommended sequencing to raise at plan time: this record's shape ruling is load-bearing for task
770, whose fix renders blocker entries into prose on the assumption they are objects. Settle the
shape here first, or fold the two together deliberately.

=== EDIT TARGET, BINDING ===

Per `rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md` this repository's `.claude/` tree is a gitignored,
disposable deploy artifact regenerated from a source store; a file hand-authored under `.claude/**`
is silently wiped by the next regeneration and the edit will appear to succeed while having no
lasting effect. Edit under the source store at the mirroring path. Re-derive it rather than
trusting this note - `source_dir` lives PER EXTENSION, not at top level:
  jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json
  jq -r '.extensions.lean.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json
A top-level `jq -r '.source_dir'` returns null; that is the key being nested, not absent. Reading
of this record's creation: `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/{core,lean}`.
After editing, redeploy with `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm the result is
a clean verify. Stage narrowly: explicit file lists only, never a directory or glob pathspec.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

- The reproduction command above exits 0 with the Validation Summary block present, OR exits with
  a documented code after printing at least one `[FAIL]` line naming the real problem. A silent
  non-zero with only PASS lines is the defect and must not survive.
- Extend the validator's test coverage (do not replace existing cases) with one string-shaped
  `blockers` fixture and one object-shaped fixture, and show the string-shaped case fails against
  the unmodified script.
- The shape ruling is recorded in the plan with its chosen authority, and whichever of the schema
  or the lean hard agent instruction is non-conforming is actually amended - not left to drift.
- The validator's header exit-code list matches its real exit paths.

=== DELIVERABLE HYGIENE ===

Every edited file is outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references
(`rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language
(`rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Cite durable anchors - file names, function
names, check names, field names, flag names - only.

=== PROVENANCE ===

Observed live in session `sess_1793823065_4dcf25`, cycle 2 of task 761, and approved at the
orchestrate-lead level as an agent-system change request. The run's detected-defect entry carries
defect_class HANDOFF_VALIDATION_FAILED, detecting_site
`skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md:cycle-postflight-handoff-validation`. The mathematical work of the
originating task closed green (full `lake build` exit 0, sorry 0, five repo gates passing); this
is a fault in the agent system, not in that work.


=== CANDIDATE DUPLICATE, NOT YET RULED (2026-11-04) ===

The source-store repository's open record #472 handoff_validator_crash_and_defect_record_gap
addresses the same validate-handoff.sh crash as this record. #472 is 15,791 characters against this
record's 8,752 and carries a second half this record does not (the defect recorder refusing every
consumer-repo attribution). This record's own promise to settle the canonical blockers shape may or
may not fall inside #472's scope, and neither record cites an entry_id, so there is no provenance
shortcut. RULING THIS PAIR REQUIRES READING BOTH IN FULL -- it was deliberately left undecided
rather than guessed from the titles. The identifier #472 is a number in THAT repository's task space
and does not resolve here.

Migrated from the BimodalLogic repository, where this record was #857 (project_name `validate_handoff_crash_and_blockers_shape`), on 2026-11-08, under the ruling that all meta records live in this repository, following
context/patterns/cross-repo-task-migration.md.

FILE SCOPE (procedure step 7): deployed .claude/** mirror entries were stripped as a consequence of the move,
not as a correction -- they were declared so the source repository overlap gate could see a collision

active_projects.title: Require task descriptions to request a proposal packet instead of instructing a dispatch to file tasks
active_projects.description:
Document the convention that a task description must ask an autonomous dispatch for a PROPOSAL PACKET, never for task FILING, because filing requires a foreground user confirmation no dispatched agent can perform.

THE DEFECT, STATED AS AN UNSATISFIABLE INSTRUCTION. A task description phrased as "let the conclusion stage file what survives" -- or any equivalent wording that directs an autonomous research/plan/implement dispatch to file follow-up tasks -- cannot be honored by the agent that receives it. `docs/reference/standards/multi-task-creation-standard.md`'s Component 7 makes user confirmation mandatory and foreground-only, and `AskUserQuestion` is categorically withheld from every dispatched subagent, so the dispatch has no route to the confirmation the standard requires. The instruction is not merely awkward; it is impossible to execute as written.

VERBATIM EVIDENCE, QUOTED FROM THE ORIGINATING ISSUE-LOG ENTRY AND NOT PARAPHRASED: "The dispatch defers task filing to 'the conclusion stage', but the Multi-Task Creation Standard's Component 7 makes user confirmation mandatory and foreground-only, so no autonomous implement dispatch can file the recommended tasks. The plan resolves this by having the implement phase render a reconciled proposal packet plus issues.jsonl follow_up_task entries instead of filing, leaving the Component 7 decision with the user."

THE COST IS REDISCOVERY, NOT FAILURE. Nothing was lost on the originating run: the dispatch noticed the conflict, invented a workaround (render a reconciled proposal packet plus `issues.jsonl` `follow_up_task` entries instead of filing), and left the Component 7 decision with the user. That is the correct behaviour. The defect is that every dispatch handed such an instruction must independently rediscover the same conflict and independently reinvent the same workaround, spending reasoning tokens on a question the system has already answered -- and a dispatch that does NOT notice will either stall at an unreachable confirmation or file tasks without the confirmation the standard requires. The originating entry's `severity: minor` and `resolution: worked_around` are both correct and should not be inflated.

THE CAPABILITY IS NOT MISSING -- ONLY THE PHRASING CONVENTION IS. Do not scope this as "add a way for dispatches to file tasks". The orchestration conclusion stage (`context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md`, Move 5) ALREADY carries the Component 7 gate: its channel (c), "follow-up tasks as children", is executed at the orchestrate-lead level where `AskUserQuestion` is reachable, and its Step 4b channel already routes agent-system change requests through a confirmed dispatch to the task-creating agent. Read "The Exactly-One-Channel Rule", "The Hint-Versus-Decision Rule", and Step 4c before writing anything. The hand-off mechanism works. What is undocumented is how a task description should PHRASE its hand-off to that mechanism: the description must ask the dispatch to produce the evidence the lead will confirm (a proposal packet, `issues.jsonl` entries with `suggested_channel`), never to perform the filing itself.

DIAGNOSE THE SITING BEFORE COMMITTING TO A REMEDY -- THIS IS DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-DECIDED. Three candidate sites, to be evaluated with evidence rather than ranked here:
  (a) The task-authoring standard. A convention stated once in `docs/reference/standards/multi-task-creation-standard.md`, adjacent to Component 7's own Foreground Requirement, saying that a task description MUST NOT instruct a dispatch to file tasks and MUST instead request a proposal packet. Weigh: that document governs the CREATION surfaces (`/task`, `/meta`, `/spawn`, the conclusion stage), so a reader composing a task description may not consult it.
  (b) The conclusion-stage contract. A statement in `context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md` that the stage consumes proposal packets and `issues.jsonl` entries, and that a task description naming this stage as the filer is malformed. Weigh: this is where the reader who wrote the offending phrasing was already looking, but the stage is only one of several consumers of such a hand-off.
  (c) The dispatch-composition path. A note emitted or embedded where a dispatch body is assembled (`scripts/orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh` and the aux/unwind variants), telling the receiving agent that filing is out of reach and a packet is wanted. Weigh: this reaches the agent at the moment of need and needs no reader discipline, but it treats a symptom of a badly-phrased description rather than preventing the phrasing.
A composition of (a) with one of (b)/(c) is acceptable. Whatever is chosen, state the rejected options on their own merits, with the reason recorded.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WORK WORTHLESS. A second, differently-worded convention. If the proposal-packet shape is already described anywhere -- check the follow-up/skeleton-plan mechanism that `conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Coexistence Boundary With the Skeleton-Plan Follow-Up Mechanism" section names, and the `follow_up_task` vocabulary in `context/formats/issue-log.md` -- then the deliverable is a POINTER to that existing shape plus the prohibition, not a fresh specification of a packet format. Establish what already exists before writing new prose.

NON-GOALS. No change to Component 7's foreground requirement or to any confirmation gate -- the requirement is correct and is the reason this convention is needed. No new capability for dispatched agents to file tasks, and no relaxation of the `AskUserQuestion` withholding. No change to the conclusion stage's channel routing, filter predicate, or exactly-one-channel rule. No retroactive rewriting of existing task descriptions that carry the offending phrasing; if a sweep for them is wanted, it is its own record.

ACCEPTANCE. (1) The convention is stated once, at a single chosen site, with pointers from the others rather than restatement. (2) It names the concrete forbidden shape (a description instructing a dispatch to file tasks) and the concrete required shape (a description requesting a proposal packet plus issue-log entries, with the filing decision left to a foreground surface). (3) It names WHY -- Component 7's foreground requirement and the subagent tool withholding -- so a future reader can re-derive the rule instead of taking it on faith. (4) Redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY -- BINDING. `.claude/**` in this repository is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from a source store; a hand edit there is silently wiped by the next regeneration and will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. The owning extension is `core`. Resolve its source store with `jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json` -- note `source_dir` is PER-EXTENSION, so a top-level `jq -r '.source_dir'` returns `null`, which must NOT be read as the key being absent; when the per-extension lookup yields nothing, the store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`. Edit at the paths mirroring the deployed ones under that store, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, then redeploy. Never hand-author under `.claude/**`.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. Every edited file lies outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Cite durable anchors only: file names, section headings, component names ("Component 7"), field names (`suggested_channel`, `follow_up_task`), and tool names (`AskUserQuestion`). The originating task number and the issue entry_id below belong in this description only, never in deliverable prose.

PROVENANCE AND CITATION. Raised by /orchestrate's conclusion stage and approved at the orchestrate-lead level as an agent-system change request, session `sess_1793900475_c93eff`. The originating issue-log entry, cited verbatim for audit against its evidence: {task 872, entry_id iss_1793901844876_M9V2B8}, in `specs/872_open_language_transfer_ledger/issues.jsonl` -- `class: design-record defect or ambiguity`, `severity: minor`, `phase: plan`, `dispatch_seq: 2`, `resolution: worked_around`, `suggested_channel: follow_up_task`, `evidence_path: .claude/docs/reference/standards/multi-task-creation-standard.md`. Read that entry verbatim before composing anything. BACKLOG-RECONCILIATION RULING, RECORDED HONESTLY: `scripts/audit-task-proposals.sh` returned only pure-semantic `duplicate-of-open` verdicts for this proposal, every one with `mechanical_class: none` and the highest at `semantic_score: 0.525` -- below any corroboration. The three nearest open records were read and each addresses a different mechanism: one closes the conclusion stage's filter predicate against `resolution: null` entries, one closes plan-authoring self-consistency gaps, and one concerns an inherited error count on a stall re-prompt. None governs how a task description phrases its hand-off to a foreground confirmation. The proposal is ruled genuinely new on that reading, not on the matcher's recall-biased output.

active_projects.title: Stop one low-specificity shared path from producing duplicate-of-open, and settle Component 7 under /orchestrate
active_projects.description:
META TASK. TWO changes to the task-creation pipeline, ONE record, because both are consumed by
the same Component 4b/Component 7 confirmation surface and both edit the same two source files:
item 1 is a mechanical tuning of the duplicate predicate, item 2 is the contract clause that
says what the confirmation gate means when no human is in the loop.

EDIT TARGET, binding. Per rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md this repository's `.claude/`
tree is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from a source store; a
hand-authored file landing under `.claude/**` is silently wiped by the next regeneration -- the
edit appears to succeed and has no lasting effect. Make every edit under the source store at the
path mirroring the deployed one. RE-DERIVE the store rather than trusting this note, but know
what re-derivation currently yields: `source_dir` lives PER-EXTENSION at
`.extensions.<name>.source_dir` in `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json`, NOT as a top-level
key. A top-level `jq -r '.source_dir'` returns null and must NOT be read as the key being absent.
Re-derive with:

  jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json

which currently yields `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`, so the edit
targets are `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/audit-task-proposals.sh`,
`agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/backlog-reconciliation.md`,
`agent-system/extensions/core/docs/reference/standards/multi-task-creation-standard.md`, and
`agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-audit-task-proposals.sh`.

=== ITEM 1 -- ONE LOW-SPECIFICITY SHARED PATH MUST NOT ALONE PRODUCE duplicate-of-open ===

MEASURED. During a multi-task creation attempt, `audit-task-proposals.sh` returned a
`duplicate-of-open` verdict for a proposal named `oriented_forest_saturation` against open task
869 (`open_modal_invariance_ray_agreement_lifting`) on `mechanical_class: overlap`,
`semantic_score: 0.43`, `shared_paths: ["FormalSystem/Semantics/README.md"]`. Inspection showed
the two are unrelated in content: 869 is open-future/open-past modal invariance along ray
agreement; the proposal was an oriented-forest Saturation lemma. The entire overlap was ONE
shared catch-all README. Disposition at the time: the proposal's declared `file_scope` was
narrowed by hand to drop `FormalSystem/Semantics/README.md`, keeping only
`FormalSystem/Semantics/TaskFrame.lean`, rather than auto-applying a fold or adding a spurious
dependency edge between unrelated records. That manual narrowing is the defect's cost: it
distorts a record's declared scope to satisfy the matcher.

RE-REPRODUCED WHILE THIS RECORD WAS BEING FILED, and this is the strongest available evidence
that the predicate is miscalibrated rather than merely unlucky. An audit of this very proposal
against the live backlog returned `duplicate-of-open` against SIX open records -- 827, 785, 822,
834, plus others -- every one of them with `mechanical_class: "none"` and `shared_paths: []`,
i.e. NO file overlap at all, on semantic scores between 0.41 and 0.48. A verdict named
"duplicate" is being emitted for records that share literally nothing mechanically and that a
reader can confirm in one glance are unrelated. The full audit document is committed as this
record's evidence; re-derive it, do not trust this summary.

WHAT THE SCRIPT ALREADY SAYS ABOUT ITSELF, and why that is not a defence. The script's own
header states plainly that Pass 2 is "a recall-biased, over-inclusive SHORTLIST" and that "THE
SCRIPT NEVER DECIDES DUPLICATION" -- a Pass-2-only verdict is "this script's own best-effort
disposition at its stated threshold", not a certified fact. That posture is correct and must be
PRESERVED: the fix is not to start suppressing records, which the header explicitly forbids. The
problem is the LABEL, not the recall. Emitting the word `duplicate-of-open` for a zero-shared-path,
0.41-semantic-score pair spends the caller's attention and, worse, trains a caller to dismiss the
verdict vocabulary wholesale -- which is precisely how a real duplicate gets filed.

DESIGN QUESTION THE RESEARCH PHASE MUST SETTLE, not a decision this record makes. Candidate
shapes, to be weighed against `context/patterns/backlog-reconciliation.md`'s False-Negative
Posture and D5 (read that document first; it owns the vocabulary and the rationale for every
existing choice):
  (a) require mechanical corroboration -- a non-`none`, non-`scope-blind` mechanical_class --
      before the `duplicate-of-open` label may be used, demoting the uncorroborated cases to a
      weaker existing verdict (`overlaps-open`) or to a new shortlist-only label;
  (b) weight a shared path by its specificity, so a catch-all (`README.md`, `index.json`,
      `manifest.json`, a directory-level entry) counts for less than a leaf source file, with
      a single low-specificity path alone insufficient for `duplicate-of-open`;
  (c) raise the semantic threshold for the uncorroborated case only, leaving the corroborated
      case where it is.
Whichever is chosen, the chosen rule belongs in `backlog-reconciliation.md` alongside the
vocabulary it constrains, and gets a regression case in
`scripts/tests/test-audit-task-proposals.sh`. NO SUPPRESSION: every corpus record must still
appear in the output with SOME verdict, per the script's standing no-suppression guarantee.

=== ITEM 2 -- COMPONENT 7 UNDER AN /orchestrate DISPATCH ===

MEASURED CONTRACT AMBIGUITY, resolved once by hand and not written down. The Multi-Task Creation
Standard's Component 7 requires foreground user confirmation before tasks are filed. Inside an
`/orchestrate` dispatch there is no foreground user to confirm, and the dispatched task's own
description can itself pre-authorize the filing (the observed wording: "file the implementation
as its own task"). The two requirements collide, and the standard is silent on the collision.

HOW IT WAS RESOLVED IN PRACTICE, which is the candidate the standard should either adopt or
explicitly reject: the dispatch treated the task description's own pre-authorization as
standing in for the Component 7 prompt, kept the full Component 4b audit evidence intact, and
RENDERED the Component 7 confirmation table into the task summary as a durable record instead
of prompting with it. The deviation was stated as an assumption in the plan's Risks table rather
than applied silently.

WHAT THIS RECORD OWES. State the resolution in
`docs/reference/standards/multi-task-creation-standard.md`'s Component 7 section: who may
pre-authorize, what artifact the confirmation table must be written into when it is not
prompted, and -- the part the hand-resolution did not settle -- whether a pre-authorization must
be explicit in the dispatched task's description or whether the `/orchestrate` context alone
suffices. Note that `meta-builder-agent` cannot call `AskUserQuestion` at all (it is withheld
from dispatched subagents), so Component 7 is ALREADY relocated upstream to `skill-meta`'s
pre-delegation stage for the `/meta` path; the clause must be consistent with that existing
relocation rather than contradict it.

=== PROVENANCE ===

Item 1: issue-log entry iss_1793896439283_Vm6ITF in
specs/865_tm_plus_lc_axiomatization_and_automaton_obstruction/issues.jsonl.
Item 2: issue-log entry iss_1793894998996_z69HrN in the same log.
Read both `what_happened` fields before planning; they are the primary record and this
description is a compression of them.

=== ORDERING ===

Depends on the open record that owns the `--audit-verdict` argv overflow
(`state_write_audit_verdict_argv_overflow`). That record's declared scope already includes
`scripts/audit-task-proposals.sh`, `context/patterns/backlog-reconciliation.md` and
`scripts/tests/test-audit-task-proposals.sh` -- three of this record's four paths -- and a live
audit of this proposal returned `duplicate-of-open` against it on `mechanical_class: overlap`
for exactly those three. The overlap is real and the two must not run concurrently. Sequence

active_projects.title: Record the load-sized bound and the diagnostic-preserving output capture on the bounded-waiter idiom
active_projects.description:
Record two conditions the bounded-waiter guidance assumes but never states: that a waiter's bound
must be sized from its writer's measured worst case under CONCURRENT AGENT LOAD rather than its
solo expected runtime, and that a bounded run's output capture must be one that preserves partial
output when the bound fires.

NOTHING IN ANY SCRIPT IS BROKEN AND THIS IS NOT A DATA-REPAIR RECORD. The deliverable is guidance
prose in the core extension's source store plus its index wiring.

=== THE TWO MEASURED FACTS ===

(1) A full `verify-deploy.sh` re-measurement, bounded at `timeout 540` and piped through
`tail -150`, was killed by its own 540s bound before producing ANY output, under concurrent
multi-agent CPU load -- many sibling `verify-deploy.sh` invocations were observed running
concurrently. It completed only on a retry bounded at 900s.

(2) That same killed run yielded ZERO diagnostic signal: the caller could not tell how far it had
got or which gate it died in, because the `tail` pipe emitted nothing. A direct file redirect
preserves partial output across a kill.

=== READ THIS BEFORE WRITING ANY PROSE: THE "RAISE IT TO 900" FRAMING IS WRONG TWICE OVER ===

The obvious reading of fact (1) is "the bound was too small, use 900." Do NOT write that. It is
wrong on two independent, checkable grounds, and both must be reflected in the guidance.

FIRST, 900 DOES NOT FIT. The Bash tool's `timeout` parameter has a documented CEILING of
`600000`ms (600s). An inner `timeout 900` inside a foreground Bash call can therefore never fire:
the harness auto-backgrounds the call at 600s at the latest, which is precisely the failure
`external-process-wait.md` Rule 1 step (2) and `bounded-build-waiter.md`'s canonical-idiom section
both already exist to prevent. A bound above ~540 is not a tuning choice available to the
foreground form at all; it is a statement that the job has left the foreground form's reach.

SECOND, AND MORE IMPORTANTLY, THE BOUND WAS KILLING THE WRONG THING. In the foreground form
(`timeout N cmd`), the bound kills the SUBJECT -- the work is destroyed when the bound fires. In
the detach-plus-waiter form (`cmd >log 2>&1 & pid=$!` then a bounded liveness wait), the bound
ends only the WAITING; the writer runs on and the log survives on disk, so an expired waiter costs
one more bounded call rather than the whole run. The measured incident used the foreground form
for a job that needs the detached one. Under the detached form a 540s waiter expiry is a non-event
and fact (2) cannot arise either, because the writer's output is already going to a file by
redirect.

So the correct resolution of fact (1) is NOT a bigger number. It is that a full `verify-deploy.sh`
run under concurrent batch load is `external-process-wait.md` Rule 1's sub-case 3b -- a job that
cannot fit under the 600s ceiling -- and sub-case 3b is already resolved, in full, by
`bounded-build-waiter.md`'s `### Sizing a Wait Near the Per-Call Ceiling` section: launch once
with a captured PID, then issue a SEQUENCE of separate bounded calls, each gated on liveness and
sized safely under the ceiling, reading the log once liveness ends. THAT SECTION IS ALREADY
CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE REWRITTEN. What is missing is only the sizing INPUT that tells a caller
they are in 3b rather than 3a.

=== THE SIZING INPUT IS THE ACTUAL GAP ===

`bounded-build-waiter.md` Rule 1 currently reads, in part, "Size `N` to the command's expected run
time, within whatever the calling tool allows." A caller reads "expected run time" as the duration
they have observed, which in practice is a solo run on an idle machine. Under a batch
orchestration, concurrent agent load is the NORMAL case rather than the exception, and the
measured spread for this one process crosses the ceiling: comfortably inside 540 solo, above 600
under load. The rule must say that the sizing input is the measured worst case under the
concurrency the job will actually meet, and that when that figure approaches or exceeds the
ceiling the job is 3b and takes the sequence form -- not a larger inner bound.

State this as a property of the sizing INPUT, governed by the EXISTING 3a/3b split. Do NOT
introduce a new numeric threshold of any kind: the 3a/3b split already decides when the sequence
form is warranted, and a second arbiter would contradict it. Any number cited for the tool
`timeout` parameter is `120000`ms (default) or `600000`ms (ceiling).

=== THE OUTPUT-CAPTURE CONDITION, AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT REFUTES THE OBVIOUS PHRASING ===

READ THIS BEFORE WRITING ANY PROSE. It is tempting to state fact (2) as "a pipe buffers, so never
pipe a bounded run." That is measurably WRONG and would be an over-broad prohibition. Measured
directly, a writer emitting 200 lines then sleeping, killed by a 3s bound, with the capture varied:

  (a) `cmd 2>&1 | tail -150 > out`   -- out is 0 bytes, 0 lines. TOTAL LOSS.
  (b) `cmd > out 2>&1`               -- out is 3692 bytes, 200 lines. FULL partial output.
  (c) `cmd 2>&1 | head -150 > out`   -- out is 2742 bytes, 150 lines. Output SURVIVED.
  (d) `cmd 2>&1 | cat > out`         -- out is 3692 bytes, 200 lines. Output SURVIVED IN FULL.

The pipe is not the mechanism. `cat` through a pipe preserved everything and `head -N` preserved
everything it had taken. The mechanism is specific to `tail -N`: it cannot know which lines are
the LAST N until the stream ends, so by its own semantics it emits nothing before EOF, and a kill
before EOF yields nothing at all. The rule to write is therefore a POSITIVE property, not a
blocklist: the capture must be one that writes incrementally and does not require end-of-stream,
for which a direct redirect to a file is the simple guaranteed form. Name `tail -N` as the
concrete violating instance WITH its mechanism, so a reader does not generalize to every pipe and
go looking for pipes to remove elsewhere.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT OF THE PIPE FORM, ALSO MEASURED. The pipeline form destroys the
`exit 124` discrimination that `external-process-wait.md` Rule 1 step (3) depends on. Measured on
the same writer, reproducibly across runs:

  `timeout 3 cmd 2>&1 | tail -150 > out`  -- the caller's `$?` is 143, PIPESTATUS is (124, 143)
  `timeout 3 cmd > out 2>&1`              -- the caller's `$?` is 124

A pipeline's exit status is its LAST command's, so the `124` that step (3) tells the caller to
read as "the bound fired, re-check state rather than reading this as a failure of the command's
subject" is not what `$?` reports; the caller sees 143 and has lost the distinction unless they
reach into `PIPESTATUS[0]`. This is worth stating because it means the pipe form degrades the
bounded-wait contract in two places at once, not just diagnostics.

=== SITING: THREE FILES, AND WHY THE THIRD IS THE ONE THAT NAMES THE GATE ===

Measured by reading the store, the generic-540 prescription the change request describes is NOT in
either pattern file in the form the request implies. Precisely:

  - `context/patterns/bounded-build-waiter.md` Rule 1 owns the local sizing rule ("Size `N` to the
    command's expected run time"). The under-load sizing input belongs HERE. Its
    `## The Canonical Idiom` section owns the `cmd >log 2>&1 & pid=$!` form; the output-capture
    condition belongs HERE, as the stated rationale for a redirect the idiom already uses.
  - `context/patterns/external-process-wait.md` carries the `540`-versus-`600` arithmetic, but its
    `timeout 540` is a `gh run watch` example and the file states explicitly that it covers "the
    case where there is no local writer to probe." A local gate run is not its case. DO NOT edit
    it; its Rule 1 sub-case 3b already points at the bounded-waiter file by name and so inherits
    whatever this record lands. This matches the standing ruling in the sibling record on this
    file family that `external-process-wait.md` carries no restatement.
  - `context/contracts/batch-gate-stage.md` is the file that actually prescribes a bound for THIS
    process. Its `## The Executable Stage Body` step 2 directs the complete `verify-deploy.sh`
    gate set -- run by `scripts/orchestrate-batch-gate.sh`, whose own header states it "Runs the
    complete verify-deploy.sh gate set EXACTLY ONCE for the whole batch" -- to be invoked via "a
    captured PID, a `kill -0` liveness loop, an outer `timeout 540` inside a single Bash tool call
    whose own `timeout` parameter is raised to `600000`."

That last prescription is the sharpest finding in this record and the reason it names a specific
file rather than only amending generic prose. It hard-codes BOTH a 540 bound AND "a single Bash
tool call" for the heaviest gate in the system, at the one site where that gate runs under
maximum batch concurrency -- exactly the conditions under which 540 was measured insufficient and
exactly where the Sizing section calls for a SEQUENCE rather than a single call. Note the
prescription is not flatly wrong: it is correct for a solo-ish run that fits, and under-specified
for the loaded run it will routinely meet. Research should decide whether the fix is to replace
"a single Bash tool call" with the sequence form by reference, or to state the load condition and
let the Sizing section's existing 3a/3b split route it. Do not resolve that by guessing here.

=== HARD SCOPE BOUNDARY: DO NOT TOUCH THE GENERATED-COPY CONTRACT BULLET ===

`bounded-build-waiter.md`'s `## Canonical Agent-Contract Bullet (Generated-Copy Source)` section
is the single authoritative source for a MUST / MUST NOT bullet pair whose MUST half names "a
captured `pid=$!`, a `kill -0` liveness loop, and an outer `timeout N`". MEASURED: the binding
string `bounded-build-waiter.md's canonical idiom VERBATIM` appears in 28 files across the
extensions tree, and `lint-agent-contracts.sh` Check H keeps every copy byte-identical by
comparing against this file. Verify with a grep for that literal string across the source store.

Both conditions in this record are plainly tempting additions to that bullet -- it already names
"an outer `timeout N`" (which this record says how to size) and it is the text agents actually
read. DO NOT ADD EITHER. Doing so converts a two-file prose change into a synchronized edit across
every carrier, gated by a blocking lint. The bullet already binds its carriers to the canonical
idiom VERBATIM and so already inherits whatever the idiom and Rule 1 say. If research concludes
the bullet genuinely must change, RAISE IT rather than executing a multi-file edit under a record
scoped and sized as a guidance change.

=== RELATIONSHIP TO THE THREE OPEN RECORDS ON THESE FILES ===

A backlog audit run at creation time returned `superset-of-open` against
`bounded_waiter_detach_form_pid_fidelity` (mechanical class `superset`, the highest semantic score
of any corpus match) and `duplicate-of-open` against `bounded_waiter_lint_beyond_rule_two` and
`bounded_block_edit_index_and_assert`. The matcher never decides duplication, so those verdicts
are a shortlist, and the ruling is recorded here rather than left implicit:

  - `bounded_waiter_detach_form_pid_fidelity` is COMPLEMENTARY, not overlapping. Its subject is
    launch-side PID fidelity -- whether the detach form's `$!` is the writer process itself -- and
    it says nothing about bound duration or output capture. This record says nothing about which
    detach form to use. They meet only in that both amend the same file's rules, and in one
    genuine adjacency worth stating once: this record's reframe pushes callers of the heaviest gate
    TOWARD the detached form, which is precisely the form whose PID fidelity that record governs.
    The two are mutually reinforcing and neither subsumes the other.
  - `bounded_waiter_lint_beyond_rule_two` is a MECHANICAL-COVERAGE record (a hook plus its tests)
    that touches this file only to record which shapes are not detectable. No prose contention.
  - `bounded_block_edit_index_and_assert` shares only `index-entries.json`.

DEPENDENCY EDGE, AND WHY AN EDGE RATHER THAN AN EXCLUSION. Those three already form a chain
(`bounded_block_edit_index_and_assert` -> `bounded_waiter_detach_form_pid_fidelity` ->
`bounded_waiter_lint_beyond_rule_two`, itself behind a completed record on `jq` reserialization of
JSON record files). This record's edits land in `bounded-build-waiter.md`, claimed by two links of
that chain, and in `index-entries.json`, claimed by a third. Per this repository's batching
discipline, shared file territory is serialized by an explicit edge rather than excluded, so this
record depends on `bounded_waiter_lint_beyond_rule_two` as the chain's current tail, extending it
to four rather than racing a fourth writer into the same two files. There is one substantive
reason beyond territory: the detach-form record's own folded-in addition edits
`### Sizing a Wait Near the Per-Call Ceiling`, the same subsection this record's 3a/3b reasoning
turns on, so landing after it means amending settled text rather than colliding in it.

=== SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY ===

`.claude/**` is a gitignored, regenerated deploy artifact; a hand edit there is wiped by the next
regeneration and will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. The owning extension is
`core`. RE-DERIVE the store rather than trusting this note -- `source_dir` lives per-extension at
`.extensions.core.source_dir`, not as a top-level key, so a top-level lookup returns null and must
not be read as the key being absent:
  jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json
It currently yields `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`, so every edit
target is `agent-system/extensions/core/**` and never a deployed `.claude/**` path, per
`rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`. Redeploy afterwards via
`bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`.

=== CROSS-REPO SITING NOTE -- A KNOWN AND ACCEPTED CONDITION ===

This record is filed in the BimodalLogic task space while its edit target resolves only under
`/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/`. That is the same deliberate, previously approved condition carried
by its three sibling records on these files, and it is load-bearing here: a dependency edge cannot
span two repositories' task spaces, so filing this record anywhere else would silently drop the
serialization that keeps four writers out of one file. A migrator should treat the siting as a
deliberate choice, not an authoring slip. Three records in the source-store repository's own task
space bear on this class and are named so a future reader finds them without a search:
`migrate_mis_sited_agent_system_tasks`, `cross_repo_source_store_gate_blindness`, and
`agent_system_task_siting_and_target_root`.

=== AN EDITING HAZARD THE IMPLEMENTER WILL VERY LIKELY HIT ===

`hooks/validate-bounded-waiter.sh` is a PreToolUse hook that blocks a command whose text supplies
three legs at once (a loop keyword, a delay call, and a process-name-matching liveness test). It
matches raw command TEXT, heredoc payloads included, so writing prose ABOUT the forbidden shape
can itself be blocked -- the sibling record on this file family documents exactly that happening
while its own description was being written via a heredoc. Reach for a non-Bash file-writing tool
for these edits rather than concluding the edit is malformed. This is a known false-positive class
and is NOT part of this record's deliverable.

=== DELIVERABLE HYGIENE ===

Every edited file lies outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references
(`rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language
(`rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Durable anchors may be cited freely: the script
names (`verify-deploy.sh`, `orchestrate-batch-gate.sh`, `lint-agent-contracts.sh`), the shell
tokens (`tail`, `head`, `cat`, `>log 2>&1`, `$!`, `kill -0`, `timeout`, `PIPESTATUS`), the rule
numbers, the sub-case labels `3a`/`3b`, and the section headings of the edited files. The
originating task number, the issue entry_id, the specific byte and line counts from the capture
measurement, and the observed concurrent-invocation count may NOT appear in the guidance prose --
they live in this record only. State each condition as what a caller does and what the shell does,
never as a narration of a past run.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

(1) `bounded-build-waiter.md` Rule 1 states that the sizing input for `N` is the writer's measured
    worst case under the concurrent load the job will actually meet, not its solo expected
    runtime, and that concurrent agent load is the normal case in a batch orchestration.
(2) It states that when that figure approaches or exceeds the ceiling the job is sub-case 3b and
    takes the `### Sizing a Wait Near the Per-Call Ceiling` sequence form -- never a larger inner
    bound. The existing 3a/3b split remains the sole arbiter of when the sequence form is
    warranted, and NO new numeric threshold is introduced anywhere.
(3) The guidance states the foreground-versus-detached consequence once: a foreground bound kills
    the subject, a detached bound ends only the waiting and leaves the log intact.
(4) `## The Canonical Idiom` states the output-capture condition as a positive property -- the
    capture must write incrementally and must not require end-of-stream -- with a direct redirect
    named as the guaranteed form, and `tail -N` named as the concrete violating instance WITH its
    mechanism (it cannot know the last N lines before EOF). It does NOT state or imply that pipes
    generally buffer or that piping is generally forbidden.
(5) The `exit 124` consequence is stated: a pipeline's status is its last command's, so the
    pipe form costs the caller step (3)'s `124` discrimination.
(6) `batch-gate-stage.md`'s complete-gate-set prescription no longer directs a bound and a single
    call that the loaded case is measured to exceed; whichever resolution research chose is
    recorded with its reason.
(7) `external-process-wait.md` is unedited and carries no restatement of either condition.
(8) The `## Canonical Agent-Contract Bullet (Generated-Copy Source)` section is byte-identical to
    its current text, every carrier copy is untouched, and `lint-agent-contracts.sh` Check H still
    passes.
(9) `index-entries.json` reflects the landed files: `line_count` for every file whose length
    changed agrees with the file as landed, and the file remains valid JSON parseable by `jq`.
(10) The guidance carries no task-number references, no record-versioning language, and none of
     the measured counts named under DELIVERABLE HYGIENE.
(11) `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` reports `RESULT=landed_verify_clean` afterwards.

=== PROVENANCE ===

Raised during orchestration of the Lean plan-gate-collision authoring-guidance record and approved
at the orchestrate-lead level as an agent-system change request, dispatched through
/orchestrate's conclusion stage agent-system channel in session `sess_1794089411_892cf6`. The
originating entry is `specs/785_lean_plan_gate_collision_authoring_guidance/issues.jsonl`,
entry_id `iss_1794090161774_0yd94u` (class `gate-collision`, severity minor, phase implement,
dispatch_seq 16). The four-form capture measurement and the `PIPESTATUS` measurement in this

active_projects.title: conclusion stage drops null-resolution issue-log entries
active_projects.description:
Close the contract gap that makes null-resolution issue-log entries invisible to the conclusion stage

THE CONCLUSION STAGE SILENTLY DROPS NULL-RESOLUTION ISSUE-LOG ENTRIES. `context/formats/issue-log.md` declares the `resolution` field optional and nullable (its field table row reads "no (nullable)", closed vocabulary `fixed_inline | worked_around | open`). `context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Filter Predicate" admits an entry into channel classification ONLY when `resolution` is `open` or `worked_around`. An entry written with `resolution: null` is therefore neither closed (`fixed_inline`, which legitimately generates no channel item) nor classified -- it reaches NO channel and is invisible to the user. Both documents are internally consistent; the gap is between them.

VERIFIED LIVE, NOT HYPOTHESIZED. `specs/749_c_bound_half_model_a_presentation_size/issues.jsonl` holds 11 entries, every one with `resolution: null` and `suggested_channel: null`. `bash .claude/scripts/orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh --aggregate --session <sid> --tasks 749` returned `proposals: 0`, `wins: 4`, `unknown_classes: 6`. Of the 11 entries, 7 are `kind: "issue"` and were all dropped: six at `severity: minor` (classes `stale-citation`, `plan-deviation`, `plan-gap`, `plan-gap`, `plan-gap`, `build-failure`) and one at `severity: costly` (class `plan-deviation`). The 4 `kind: "win"` entries surfaced correctly, which confirms the aggregator is behaving exactly as written -- this is a contract mismatch, not an aggregator bug. Re-derive these counts from the live log rather than trusting them; they are a snapshot.

DECIDE AND LAND ONE OF THREE. (a) Make `resolution` REQUIRED at write time in `scripts/issue-record.sh`, so an entry cannot be recorded without one -- closes the hole at the writer, but every existing null-resolution entry across the repo stays invisible. (b) Widen the Filter Predicate to treat null-or-absent `resolution` as `open` -- the conservative reading, since an issue recorded without a resolution is an unresolved one; note this alone would have pushed 7 entries from ONE task into channel classification, so weigh proposal volume before choosing it. (c) Keep both contracts as they are and have the conclusion stage report a separate "unclassifiable (no resolution)" tally beside its unknown-class tally, so the entries are at least visible rather than dropped. Options (a) and (c) are composable; (b) subsumes neither. Whichever is chosen, the two documents MUST end up agreeing in writing -- the acceptance condition for this record is that a reader of either file can predict the other's behavior.

ALSO IN SCOPE. `suggested_channel` was null on all 7 dropped entries too. `conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Hint-Versus-Decision Rule" treats that field as a hint the orchestrator may override visibly, which presumes a hint exists; decide whether a null hint is acceptable or whether the writer should require one, and say so in the same place the `resolution` decision is recorded.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. All four file_scope paths live in a deployed, regenerated tree -- a hand edit under `.claude/**` is wiped by the next deploy and the edit will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. Implementation MUST resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` for the owning extension (`core`, whose source store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`) and edit at the mirroring paths there, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, then redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`. The deployed paths are declared in file_scope only so the overlap gate can see the collision surface; they are not the edit target.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. The edited files are not under `specs/**`, so the prose must carry no task-number references and no record-versioning language; cite durable anchors (file names, section headings, field names) only.

RELATED RECORDS, FOR ORIENTATION AND NOT AS DEPENDENCY EDGES. The roadmap-generator record covering `roadmap-integration.sh`'s partial-write behavior is the sibling core-extension defect with the same source-store boundary, and the file_scope-declaration-hygiene record covers a different blindness in the same admission machinery. No dependency edge to either -- nothing here blocks on them.

=== DISPOSITION PENDING 2026-11-04 -- DO NOT DISPATCH, DO NOT ABANDON YET ===

The underlying defect is FIXED. Verified in this repository's deployed tree 2026-11-04:
context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md now states that a null or omitted `resolution` is read
identically to `open`, and `implicit_open_count` is present in both that contract and the live
output of orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh --aggregate (observed returning 6 the same day). The
source-store repository's record #373 null_resolution_entries_unreachable_by_conclusion_stage,
which did that work, is `completed` with 3 artifacts.

ABANDONMENT IS RULED CORRECT BUT IS BLOCKED ON A PRECONDITION THAT CANNOT BE MET AS WRITTEN. The
migration record in that repository requires transplanting two items this record holds into the
absorbing record FIRST, and adds an explicit fail-safe: if the transplant is not possible for any
reason encountered, do NOT abandon -- report it and leave the record open. The absorbing record
#373 is CLOSED and archived, so there is no live record to amend. Checked 2026-11-04: #373 carries
no "FOLDED IN" marker, so the transplant has never happened.

This record therefore STAYS OPEN under that fail-safe. The question of where a transplant goes when
the absorbing record is already closed is now recorded on that repository's #481, which must settle
it; the identifiers #373, #390 and #481 are numbers in THAT repository's task space and do not
resolve here.


=== MIGRATION PROVENANCE (appended on migration; every line above this marker is the record verbatim) ===
Migrated from the BimodalLogic repository, where this record was #753 (project_name `conclusion_stage_drops_null_resolution_entries`), on 2026-11-08, under the ruling that all meta records live in this repository, following
context/patterns/cross-repo-task-migration.md.

FILE SCOPE (procedure step 6, DERIVED): this record declared only deployed .claude/** paths. The scope above
resolves each to its core-extension source mirror; every path was verified to exist here before being written.

DUPLICATE ASSESSMENT CARRIED FORWARD, NOT YET DISCHARGED. The migration record that owns this move assessed
this record as a deep duplicate of this repository own `null_resolution_entries_unreachable_by_conclusion_stage`
-- both analyse the identical defect to line level across issue-record.sh optional --resolution and its
`if [ -n "$resolution_arg" ]` guard, issue-log.md "no (nullable)" row, orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh
coercion of null to "", and conclusion-stage.md Filter Predicate leaving null unaddressed. That assessment
concluded this record should be ABANDONED, but only AFTER transplanting two things it holds that the absorbing
record does not. THE TRANSPLANT IS STILL OWED:
  (i) An independent second reproduction from a different run, including one entry at `costly` severity, plus
      the proposal-volume datum that one option alone would have pushed 7 entries from a single task into
      classification. Re-derive those counts from the live log rather than trusting the snapshot in the text above.
  (ii) A LIVE DISAGREEMENT, not merely extra evidence: on `suggested_channel` being null, the two records reach
      OPPOSITE conclusions. The absorbing record calls it benign and treats it as settled; the text above asks
      whether a null hint is acceptable at all, observing that the Hint-Versus-Decision Rule presumes a hint
      exists. Surface it there as OPEN rather than discarding it.
Both records now live in this repository, so the merge can be decided here. Do not abandon this record until
the transplant lands; if amending the absorbing record proves impossible, leave this one open and report why.

active_projects.title: Make the extension repo registry usable for deploy enumeration: rule between refusing test-fixture registration and pruning on read
active_projects.description:
The cross-repo extension registry at ~/.local/share/nvim/neotex-ai/extension-repo-registry.json is unusable as a deploy-enumeration source. Measured 2026-11-08: 313 entries, of which 311 are /tmp paths and only 2 are real repositories (/home/benjamin/Projects/BimodalLogic and /home/benjamin/Projects/Logos/Theory). The /tmp entries are genuine test-fixture residue -- agent scratchpad trees (/tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/wt435-pre, .../opencode-test/e2e_project) and `mktemp -d` deploy fixtures (/tmp/tmp.00uM2fRkwI/deployed, /tmp/tmp.0k6Zm9RlyP/fixture) -- written by test runs that loaded an extension into a temporary project directory. For comparison, a bounded filesystem scan (`find $HOME -maxdepth 5 -name .claude-extensions.json`) finds 16 repositories carrying a deploy manifest.

Consequence: any consumer that needs to enumerate deployed repos -- a before/after measurement, a fleet-wide sweep, or a control set -- cannot use the registry and must fall back to filesystem enumeration. The immediate consumer already worked around this: the orphan-sweep plan at specs/369_orphan_sweep_for_removed_merge_target_entries/plans/01_orphan-sweep-hook-registrations.md specifies filesystem enumeration rather than the registry as its control-set source. The workaround is in place, so this is not urgent; what remains unfixed is the registry itself.

DECIDE between two candidate shapes rather than assuming one:
(1) Refuse test-fixture registration at write time, so /tmp paths never enter the registry. Addresses the cause; leaves the existing 311 stale entries needing a one-off cleanup. Open sub-question the task must answer: what the refusal predicate actually keys on. A bare /tmp prefix test is the obvious candidate but is not obviously right -- it would also reject a legitimate project a user happens to keep under /tmp, and it would not catch a fixture rooted elsewhere (TMPDIR pointed at a non-/tmp path, or a scratchpad under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR). Consider instead keying on the fixture's own marker, or on an explicit opt-out the test harness sets, and rule on which is defensible.
(2) Prune non-existent and /tmp-anchored entries on read or on a maintenance pass. Self-healing, but keeps writing entries that will later be discarded.
A combination is plausible and should be considered on its merits, not excluded by default.

GROUNDING the task must not re-derive, and must not duplicate: shape (2) is PARTIALLY BUILT ALREADY. `M.prune_unreachable()` exists at lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/repo_registry.lua:182 and removes every registered row whose directory no longer exists on disk. It is wired, but only from one site -- lua/neotex/plugins/ai/claude/commands/picker/init.lua:343 -- inside the interactive `Global Update` picker action, and only when that action has already observed at least one unreachable row (`if #unreachable > 0 then`). So the pruning MECHANISM is not the gap; its TRIGGER is. Nothing prunes on read (`M.read()` at repo_registry.lua:57 returns the file as-is), which is why 311 dead fixture rows have accumulated. Scoping shape (2) as "write prune_unreachable" would be rework; the real shape-(2) question is whether `M.read()`, `M.list()`, or a scheduled maintenance pass should call it, and what that costs on every read.

The registration write path is `M.upsert()` at repo_registry.lua:114, called via `pcall(repo_registry.upsert, project_dir, extension_name)` from lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/init.lua:736 on every successful extension load. `M.upsert` already has one exclusion precedent to follow rather than invent: the HOST-REPO EXCLUSION (`M.is_host_repo`, repo_registry.lua:46), which returns early with success and registers nothing. A shape-(1) fixture exclusion is structurally the same move and should match that shape, including its non-fatal posture -- a registry refusal must never fail an otherwise-successful extension load.

SCOPE NOTE: the registry file itself is runtime state under ~/.local/share/nvim/, not source-controlled content. The fix lands in the Lua code that writes and reads it -- repo_registry.lua, and picker/init.lua if the prune trigger moves -- never in the registry JSON as a checked-in artifact. The one-off cleanup of the 311 existing stale entries is a runtime-state operation, not a repo edit, and should be specified as such (a documented one-shot invocation, not a committed file change).

TASK TYPE RATIONALE: filed as task_type `neovim`, not `meta`. The change request reached this backlog through the agent-system channel, but the implementation site is plain Neovim Lua under lua/neotex/plugins/ai/, so `neovim` routing (neovim-research-agent / planner-agent / neovim-implementation-agent) is the honest routing. No file under .claude/** or agent-system/extensions/** is in scope.

BACKLOG RECONCILIATION, already run (scripts/audit-task-proposals.sh, verdict recorded on this entry's audit_verdict field): the mechanically-corroborated matches are closed tasks that BUILT this registry, not ones that fixed it. Task 45 ("Picker fixes: Global Update extension-repo registry, and honest [Reload All]/[Regenerate] entries", mechanical_class subset, discharging_artifact null) and task 22 created repo_registry.lua and prune_unreachable itself -- task 22's plan records both as completed checklist items. Neither addressed test-fixture pollution or the prune trigger, so this is a follow-up defect on closed work, not a duplicate of it. The 15 duplicate-of-open verdicts are all pure-semantic with mechanical_class "none", no shared paths, and scores 0.42-0.52; per the matcher's own stated posture these are recall-biased shortlist noise, and none concerns the registry.

EVIDENCE CITATION: recorded during task 369's plan phase as issue-log entry iss_1794210505854_rff529 (class: tooling, severity: minor) in specs/369_orphan_sweep_for_removed_merge_target_entries/issues.jsonl.
